# HOK-1539: Add config setting to log info

# Add config setting to log info - Quick Reference

**Issue ID**: HOK-1539

## Objective

When the wavemill autonomous workflow logs a notable behavior that is governed by a config setting (e.g., "Window stays open for review - close it when ready"), the log line should include the controlling config setting name and current value (e.g., `(autoClose=false)`) so users know exactly which knob to change. Audit existing active log statements in `shared/lib/` and identify the small set of behaviors that are config-driven and user-relevant, then annotate them — without making logs noisy for non-config-driven messages.

## Key Files

* `shared/lib/wavemill-common.sh`
* `shared/lib/wavemill-mill.sh`
* `shared/lib/wavemill-startup-runner.sh`
* `shared/lib/config.ts`
* `tools/prompts/issue-writer.md` (audit reference only — do not modify)

## Critical Constraints

1. Annotate only log lines that describe behavior controlled by a documented config setting; do not annotate every log statement (avoid noise).
2. Use a single, consistent annotation format: `(<settingPath>=<value>)` appended to the existing message — do not change message wording.
3. Resolve setting values through existing config loaders (`loadWavemillConfig` for TypeScript, established shell helpers for bash) — do not re-implement config reading.

## Success Criteria (High-Level)

- [ ] The "Window stays open for review" log line includes the controlling config setting and its current value
- [ ] At least 2–3 other config-driven log lines in active code paths receive the same annotation pattern, identified via an explicit audit
- [ ] An audit document (or commit description) lists each candidate log line, the setting path, and a keep/skip decision with rationale
- [ ] No new log lines are added; only existing ones are annotated
- [ ] Tests and lint pass; manual verification confirms annotated format renders correctly with both default and overridden config values
- [ ] PR created and linked to HOK-1539

## Detailed Sections

Full details available on-demand in [task-packet-details.md](<http://task-packet-details.md>):

* [Section 1: Complete Objective & Scope](<#1-objective>)
* [Section 2: Technical Context](<#2-technical-context>)
* [Section 3: Implementation Approach](<#3-implementation-approach>)
* [Section 4: Success Criteria](<#4-success-criteria>)
* [Section 5: Implementation Constraints](<#5-implementation-constraints>)
* [Section 6: Validation Steps](<#6-validation-steps>)
* [Section 7: Definition of Done](<#7-definition-of-done>)
* [Section 8: Rollback Plan](<#8-rollback-plan>)
* [Section 9: Release Readiness](<#9-release-readiness>)
* [Section 10: Proposed Labels](<#10-proposed-labels>)

**Implementation Note**: Start with this overview. Read detailed sections on-demand as you implement.

---

## 1\. Objective

### What

Annotate user-facing log lines in the wavemill workflow whose behavior is governed by a config setting, by appending `(<settingPath>=<currentValue>)` to the existing message — starting with the "Window stays open for review - close it when ready" line, then sweeping the active code paths for similar opportunities.

### Why

When the autonomous workflow exhibits a notable behavior (e.g., a tmux pane stays open after completion), users frequently don't know that this behavior is configurable, what the setting is called, or where to change it. Embedding the setting name and current value in the log itself eliminates a documentation-lookup step and makes the system self-describing.

### Scope In

* Locate the exact "Window stays open for review - close it when ready" log statement (or the closest match) in `shared/lib/` and identify the controlling config setting.
* Append `(<settingPath>=<currentValue>)` to that log line, where `<settingPath>` is the dotted JSON path in `.wavemill-config.json` and `<currentValue>` is the resolved effective value.
* Audit other log statements in `shared/lib/wavemill-*.sh`, `shared/lib/wavemill-*.ts`, `tools/`, and `commands/` that describe behavior controlled by an existing setting in `wavemill-config.schema.json`.
* For each candidate, decide keep/skip and document the rationale in the PR description (or a short audit note in `docs/`).
* Annotate the kept candidates using the same format.
* Add tests for any new helper introduced (e.g., a small `formatConfigAnnotation()` utility), and update at least one existing test that captures log output if such tests exist.

### Scope Out

* **No new log lines**: Do not introduce additional logs to highlight settings.
* **No log-level changes**: Do not promote/demote `info` ↔ `debug`.
* **No config schema changes**: Do not add new settings or rename existing ones.
* **No formatting overhauls**: Do not restructure or reword existing log messages beyond appending the annotation.
* **No annotation of behavior that is not config-driven**: e.g., do not annotate "Branch created" with the branch name as if it were a setting.
* **No annotation of high-frequency / per-tool logs** (e.g., per-PreToolUse hook events) — those would create noise.
* **No changes to Codex prompt files** (`codex/prompts/*.md`) unless they contain active runtime log statements (they do not).

---

## 2\. Technical Context

### Repository

This work happens in the wavemill repo (current working directory). All changes stay within this repo.

### Key Files

**Primary candidate (mentioned in issue):**

* `shared/lib/wavemill-startup-runner.sh` — likely owns the "window stays open" message via tmux pane lifecycle.
* `shared/lib/wavemill-common.sh` — common shell helpers; may host the existing config-reading helpers.
* `shared/lib/wavemill-mill.sh` — mill-mode lifecycle; second likely candidate for the "window stays open" message.

**Audit surface (logs in active runtime paths):**

* `shared/lib/*.sh` — all active shell library files (`agent-adapters.sh`, `wavemill-status.sh`, `tend-controller.ts` companion logs, etc.).
* `shared/lib/*.ts` — active TypeScript runtime modules that emit `console.log/info/warn` (e.g., `eval-orchestrator.ts`, `llm-cli.ts`, `workflow-router.ts`, `promotion-controller.ts`, `tend-controller.ts`).
* `tools/*.ts` — CLI wrappers; check for top-level info logs about behavior modes.

**Config sources:**

* `wavemill-config.schema.json` — authoritative list of settings (use this as the source of truth for `<settingPath>` strings).
* `shared/lib/config.ts` — `loadWavemillConfig`, `getRouterConfig`, `getEvalConfig`, etc.

**Reference (do not modify):**

* `tools/prompts/issue-writer.md`

### Relevant Subsystem Specs

* **router** (`.wavemill/context/router.md`)
  * **Key Constraints**: Always prepend degraded-mode rationale to routing decisions when constrained or survival; treat constrained/survival as aggregate-across-frontier states. The existing rationale-prepending pattern is precedent for "annotating output with the reason behind a decision" — follow the same spirit here.
  * **Known Failure Modes**: N/A for log annotation.
  * **Testing Patterns**: Test helpers (`writeQuotaState`) inject state; reuse the same approach if any annotated log is router-related.
* **eval-system** (`.wavemill/context/eval-system.md`)
  * **Key Constraints**: Schema evolution must be additive. This task does not change the eval schema, but if any annotated log writes to eval records, ensure the change is purely textual.
  * **Known Failure Modes**: Older eval readers rejecting records — irrelevant here because no schema change.
  * **Testing Patterns**: For TypeScript log-emitting modules, use temp repos and assert on captured stdout/stderr.
* **quota-tracking** (`.wavemill/context/quota-tracking.md`)
  * **Testing Patterns**: Simulate state via helpers; useful pattern for any annotated log whose value comes from quota-driven config.

### Dependencies

* Existing config loaders: `shared/lib/config.ts` (TypeScript) and shell helpers in `shared/lib/wavemill-common.sh` (bash).
* `wavemill-config.schema.json` for canonical setting paths.
* No external dependencies, no new packages.

### Architecture Notes

* **Annotation format**: Single dotted-path setting name followed by `=` and the resolved value, in parentheses, appended after a single space:
  * `Window stays open for review - close it when ready (workflow.autoClose=false)`
  * Use the JSON path exactly as it appears in `wavemill-config.schema.json`.
  * Boolean values render as `true`/`false`; numbers as their decimal form; strings without quotes; arrays/objects should not be annotated (skip those candidates — too noisy).
* **Resolution**: Always resolve the *effective* value (post defaults), not the raw config. In TypeScript use `loadWavemillConfig(repoDir)`; in bash use the existing `wavemill_config_get` (or equivalent) helper if one exists, else add a tiny local helper that uses `jq` against `.wavemill-config.json` with a hardcoded default fallback.
* **Helper placement**: If a small formatting helper is warranted (likely yes for TS, optional for bash), place it in `shared/lib/log-annotations.ts` (new) or co-locate as a private function in the consuming module. Prefer co-location unless reused 3+ times.

---

## 3\. Implementation Approach

1. **Locate the seed log line.** Grep for `"Window stays open"` and `"close it when ready"` (case-insensitive) across `shared/`, `tools/`, `commands/`. Record the exact file and line(s).
2. **Identify the controlling setting.** Trace the flag/branch that gates the "stays open vs auto-close" behavior back to its config source. Record the dotted path as it appears in `wavemill-config.schema.json` (e.g., `workflow.autoClose` or whatever the actual path is — confirm before assuming).
3. **Audit additional candidates.** Grep `shared/lib/*.sh` and `shared/lib/*.ts` for `console.log`, `console.info`, `echo`, `printf`, and `log_info`/`log_warn` calls. For each, ask: "Is the behavior described here turned on/off or shaped by a config setting in `wavemill-config.schema.json`?" Build a candidate list with: file:line, message, controlling setting (or "none"), keep/skip decision, rationale.
4. **Define the annotation format and helper.**
   * Format: ` (<settingPath>=<value>)` — leading space, single setting per log line, no nested objects, value rendered via `JSON.stringify`-style for primitives but unquoted for strings (e.g., `mode=normal` not `mode="normal"`).
   * TypeScript helper (if 2+ TS sites): `formatConfigAnnotation(path: string, value: unknown): string` returning `` ` (${path}=${rendered})` ``. Place in `shared/lib/log-annotations.ts`.
   * Bash helper (if 2+ bash sites): add `wavemill_format_config_annotation` near the existing config helper in `wavemill-common.sh`.
5. **Apply annotations to the kept candidates.** Edit each log site to append the annotation. Resolve the value at log time (do not cache stale values across the lifecycle).
6. **Add unit tests.**
   * For the helper(s): verify rendering of `true`, `false`, numbers, strings, and that arrays/objects either throw or return empty (matching whatever you choose).
   * For each annotated log: a single end-to-end-style assertion that the resulting line contains the expected `(=<value>)` substring with both the default and an overridden value.
7. **Document the audit.** Add a brief table to the PR description (or a short note in `docs/` if it warrants persistence) listing every candidate considered and the keep/skip decision. This makes it easy for the reviewer to verify nothing user-relevant was missed and nothing trivial was over-annotated.
8. **Run the full test/lint matrix** and self-verify by running a wavemill flow that triggers the seed log line under both `autoClose=true` and `autoClose=false`.

---

## 4\. Success Criteria

### Functional Requirements

- [ ] **\[REQ-F1\]** The log statement matching "Window stays open for review - close it when ready" (or its current exact wording) emits a line ending in ` (<settingPath>=<currentValue>)` where `<settingPath>` is the dotted JSON path of the controlling config and `<currentValue>` is the effective value at log time.
- [ ] **\[REQ-F2\]** At least 2 additional config-driven log lines in active runtime paths under `shared/lib/` (TS or shell) are annotated with the same `(path=value)` suffix format. The exact set is documented in the PR description.
- [ ] **\[REQ-F3\]** A single annotation helper is used consistently across all annotated TypeScript sites (or each bash site uses the same inline pattern). Rendering is identical for identical inputs across sites.
- [ ] **\[REQ-F4\]** When the user changes the controlling config value in `.wavemill-config.json`, the next emission of an annotated log line reflects the new value (no caching across config reloads).
- [ ] **\[REQ-F5\]** No log line that does NOT correspond to a config-driven behavior is annotated. The audit table in the PR description shows at least 3 candidates that were considered and explicitly rejected with rationale.

### Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] No annotation increases log frequency (no new emit sites).
- [ ] Annotation suffix adds < 80 characters to any single log line in typical config states.
- [ ] No measurable startup-time regression (config is already loaded; annotation is a string concat).

### Code Quality

- [ ] Follows existing codebase patterns (thin tool / shared lib split).
- [ ] TypeScript types correct, no `any` unless justified.
- [ ] No lint errors (`pnpm lint` or repo equivalent).
- [ ] No shellcheck regressions in modified `.sh` files (if shellcheck is part of the existing test pipeline).

---

## 5\. Implementation Constraints

* **Code style**: Match surrounding style. For TS, use existing import patterns from `shared/lib/config.ts`. For bash, use the same logging conventions and quoting style already present in the file you edit.
* **Format consistency**: Always ` (=<value>)` with a single leading space, parentheses, `=` separator, no quotes around string values, no whitespace inside parens. Never use `[]` or `:` instead.
* **Single source of truth**: Setting paths must match `wavemill-config.schema.json` exactly. If the schema uses `workflow.autoClose`, do not write `workflow.auto_close` or `autoClose`.
* **Effective values only**: Always log the post-defaults effective value, not the raw on-disk value. This is what `loadWavemillConfig()` already returns.
* **No new settings**: This task does not introduce config keys. If you find a behavior that *should* be configurable but isn't, note it in the PR description for follow-up — do not implement it here.
* **Noise budget**: If audit yields >6 candidates, keep the top 3–5 by user impact and explicitly defer the rest with rationale.
* **Testing**: Integration-style tests should hit real config loading, not mocks (per project feedback that mocked configs have masked drift).
* **Backwards compatibility**: Log messages are not API; appending an annotation is non-breaking. Do not, however, modify existing log message wording.
* **Security**: Never log values that could plausibly be secrets. If a candidate setting contains `token`, `key`, `secret`, `password`, or `credential` in its path, redact the value as `<redacted>` instead.

---

## 6\. Validation Steps

### Functional Requirement Validation

**\[REQ-F1\] Seed log line is annotated**

Validation scenario:

1. Setup: From the worktree root, set the controlling config to its non-default value (e.g., `autoClose=false`) in `.wavemill-config.json`.
2. Action: Run the wavemill flow that produces the "Window stays open for review" message and capture stdout/stderr to a file.
3. Expected result: The line matches the regex `Window stays open for review.*\(<settingPath>=false\)$` where `<settingPath>` is the actual confirmed path (e.g., `workflow.autoClose`).
4. Edge cases:
   * Setting absent from `.wavemill-config.json` (relying on defaults) → annotation shows the default value, not the literal string `undefined`.
   * Setting set to `true` → log line either does not appear (because behavior is suppressed) OR appears with `=true` if it still triggers; whichever matches current code, it must be self-consistent.

**\[REQ-F2\] Additional config-driven log lines are annotated**

Validation scenario:

1. Setup: Identify two additional log sites annotated by this PR from the audit table.
2. Action: For each, trigger the code path and capture output.
3. Expected result: Each line ends with ` (=<value>)` and the path appears verbatim in `wavemill-config.schema.json`.
4. Edge cases:
   * Override the setting in `.wavemill-config.json` and rerun → annotation reflects the override.
   * Boolean setting → renders as `true`/`false` (lowercase, no quotes).

**\[REQ-F3\] Consistent helper usage**

Validation scenario:

1. Setup: Inspect the diff.
2. Action: For TypeScript sites, confirm all use the same helper (`formatConfigAnnotation` or chosen name). For bash sites, confirm all use the same inline pattern or shared helper.
3. Expected result: No two sites format the annotation differently.
4. Edge cases:
   * String value with embedded space → still renders without quotes; spaces preserved.
   * Numeric value → renders as decimal, no scientific notation for typical config numbers.

**\[REQ-F4\] Live value reflects current config**

Validation scenario:

1. Setup: Run the workflow once with default config; capture output.
2. Action: Change the setting in `.wavemill-config.json`, run again, capture output.
3. Expected result: The annotation in the second run reflects the new value, not the cached first-run value.
4. Edge cases:
   * Config cache cleared between runs → expected new value.
   * Same process re-running the path → if `loadWavemillConfig` caches per-process, the test should verify that the path still resolves the value correctly within the same lifecycle (acceptable to use cached value within one run).

**\[REQ-F5\] No over-annotation**

Validation scenario:

# HOK-1544: Tend challenge gate has a registration race; primary can merge before challenger is registered

# Tend Challenge Gate Registration Race - Quick Reference

**Issue ID**: HOK-1544

## Objective

Fix the registration race in tend's challenge gate that allows the primary PR of a challenge pair to merge into `auto/integration` before the challenger task is registered in workflow state. Add a Linear-backed cross-check (Plan A) so the gate can recognize in-flight pair members independent of `workflow-state.json`, with a branch-name heuristic (Plan B) as a fallback for when Linear is unavailable.

## Key Files

* `shared/lib/tend-challenge-gate.ts`
* `shared/lib/tend-controller.ts`
* `shared/lib/linear.js`
* `shared/lib/tend-controller.test.ts`
* `shared/lib/tend-challenge-gate.test.ts`

## Critical Constraints

1. The gate MUST hold a primary PR when *any* signal — workflow state, Linear sibling issue, or branch-name twin — implies a challenger exists, even if the challenger PR is not yet open.
2. Linear and gh lookups MUST fail closed: if the lookup errors or times out for a wavemill-launched PR, the gate holds the PR rather than letting it through (avoids re-introducing the race silently).
3. Existing tend behavior for non-paired PRs (single-task PRs with no challenger sibling) MUST remain unchanged — no extra latency, no spurious holds.

## Success Criteria (High-Level)

- [ ] Gate holds primary PR when challenger task is in workflow state but challenger PR is not yet open
- [ ] Gate holds primary PR when only a Linear sibling issue (challenger identifier) exists, not yet in workflow state
- [ ] Gate holds primary PR when only a `task/<slug>-challenger` (or twin) branch exists on origin
- [ ] All existing `tend-controller` tests remain green; new regression test reproduces HOK-1523 timing
- [ ] PR created and linked to HOK-1544

## Detailed Sections

Full details available on-demand in [task-packet-details.md](<http://task-packet-details.md>):

* [Section 1: Complete Objective & Scope](<#1-objective>)
* [Section 2: Technical Context](<#2-technical-context>)
* [Section 3: Implementation Approach](<#3-implementation-approach>)
* [Section 4: Success Criteria](<#4-success-criteria>)
* [Section 5: Implementation Constraints](<#5-implementation-constraints>)
* [Section 6: Validation Steps](<#6-validation-steps>)
* [Section 7: Definition of Done](<#7-definition-of-done>)
* [Section 8: Rollback Plan](<#8-rollback-plan>)
* [Section 9: Release Readiness](<#9-release-readiness>)
* [Section 10: Proposed Labels](<#10-proposed-labels>)

**Implementation Note**: Start with this overview. Read detailed sections on-demand as you implement.

---

## 1\. Objective

### What

Close the registration race in `shared/lib/tend-challenge-gate.ts` so that the primary PR of a challenge pair cannot be merged into `auto/integration` while the challenger task is still in the process of registering. Add Linear-based and branch-name-based detection so the gate has authoritative pair information even when `workflow-state.json` is incomplete.

### Why

On 2026-05-04 (incident HOK-1523), PR #497 (primary) merged into `auto/integration` at 19:02:24, then 16 minutes later the challenge comparison ran and selected challenger #501 as the winner — but #497 was already merged. Both PRs ended up in `auto/integration` and queued for promotion to `main`, breaking the "only one side wins" guarantee of the challenge system. Significant code overlap (in `shared/lib/migration-ast.ts`, `shared/lib/ready-stage.ts`) plus 11 dead test fixtures from the loser would pollute `main`. The gate currently relies entirely on `workflow-state.json`, which can be stale when challenger and primary launch at slightly different times.

### Scope In

* Add a Linear sibling-issue lookup helper in `shared/lib/linear.js` for "list open issues by identifier prefix" (e.g., `HOK-1523` → returns siblings like `HOK-1523_c` if pairing convention uses suffix, OR a sibling issue with a `challenge-of` link/label)
* Update `shared/lib/tend-challenge-gate.ts` to consult Linear AND branch-name twin existence in addition to workflow state
* Update `shared/lib/tend-controller.ts` only as needed to pass repo/Linear context into the gate
* Add regression test in `shared/lib/tend-controller.test.ts` (or a new `shared/lib/tend-challenge-gate.test.ts` if cleaner) that simulates the HOK-1523 timing window
* Fail-closed semantics: when Linear/gh lookups error, hold wavemill-launched PRs rather than letting them through
* Document the new gate signals briefly in JSDoc on the exported gate function

### Scope Out

* Cleaning up the 11 dead test fixtures from #497 (`tests/fixtures/migrations/*.py`) — explicitly listed as a separate follow-up task in the issue
* Reverting #497 or #501 — that's a separate `auto/integration` cleanup task
* Implementing the cool-off window (Plan C) — only build it if A+B prove insufficient
* Changing how challenger tasks register into workflow state in the first place
* Modifying `auto/integration` promotion logic or `promotion-controller.ts`
* Restructuring the workflow-state.json schema

---

## 2\. Technical Context

### Repository

This work happens in the wavemill repo (current working directory). The bug surfaces in the tend controller path, which evaluates open PRs and decides which are eligible to merge into `auto/integration`.

### Key Files

| File | Role | Action |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `shared/lib/tend-challenge-gate.ts` | Main gate logic; reads workflow state via `loadWorkflowStateChallengePairs()` at lines 118-130 per issue | Modify: add Linear and branch-twin signals |
| `shared/lib/tend-controller.ts` | Calls `applyChallengePairGates` around line 200 | Modify: ensure gate has access to repoDir / Linear client / git origin info |
| `shared/lib/linear.js` | Existing Linear API client (exports `getIssue`, `fetchBacklog`) | Modify: add `listOpenIssuesByIdentifierPrefix(prefix)` helper |
| `shared/lib/tend-controller.test.ts` | Existing tend controller tests | Modify: add regression tests for the race window |
| `shared/lib/tend-challenge-gate.test.ts` | New file (only if isolating the gate logic makes the test cleaner) | Create only if needed |

### Relevant Subsystem Specs

> ⚠️ **Knowledge Gap**: No subsystem specs found for the tend controller, challenge gate, or workflow-state systems specifically. The provided specs (`router.md`, `eval-system.md`, `quota-tracking.md`) are not directly relevant to this bug. After implementation, consider running `wavemill context init --force` to create a subsystem spec for the tend / challenge-gate subsystem so future tasks have authoritative documentation of pair-gating semantics.

### Dependencies

* Existing Linear API client at `shared/lib/linear.js` — already provides `getIssue()` and `fetchBacklog()`. The new `listOpenIssuesByIdentifierPrefix()` helper should use the same auth pathway.
* `gh` CLI for branch-twin existence check via `git ls-remote origin task/<slug>-challenger` (or equivalent), invoked through `shared/lib/shell-utils.ts`'s safe-exec helper.
* Workflow state file `workflow-state.json` (already consumed by current gate) — keep using it as the first signal.
* The recent merge commit `eaaec87` modified `shared/lib/tend-controller.ts` and `shared/lib/tend-controller.test.ts` for an unrelated promote checks fix; do not regress those changes.

### Architecture Notes

* The challenge-pair system records pairs in `workflow-state.json` and emits comparison records to `challenge-records.jsonl`. The gate sits before the merge step in tend's pipeline.
* Pair naming convention (per the issue): primary identifier is `HOK-1523`, challenger identifier is `HOK-1523_c`. Both live under the same root Linear ID. Confirm this convention in `shared/lib/linear.js` and any pair-registration code before relying on it; if the convention is different (e.g., a separate Linear issue with a "challenge-of" link), follow what's actually in the code.
* Branch convention (per the issue): `task/<slug>` (primary) and `task/<slug>-challenger` (challenger). Confirm in current branch creation code paths before relying on it.
* Follow the thin-tools / shared-lib pattern: business logic stays in `shared/lib/`; no new top-level tool needed.
* Use `mutateJsonState` / `state_mutate` only if writing to JSON state — this task should be read-only for state.

---

## 3\. Implementation Approach

1. **Verify pair conventions in the current code.** Before implementing, grep the codebase for how challenger identifiers and challenger branches are actually constructed. Look at challenge-pair registration code, any pair-creation helpers, and existing `tend-challenge-gate.ts` lines 118-130 to confirm the exact identifier/branch naming convention. Adjust the implementation to match what's actually used (the issue's examples — `HOK-1523_c` and `task/<slug>-challenger` — are illustrative; confirm before encoding).
2. **Add** `listOpenIssuesByIdentifierPrefix()` to `shared/lib/linear.js`. Accepts a Linear identifier (e.g., `HOK-1523`) and returns all open Linear issues whose identifier matches the pair convention used by wavemill (e.g., starts with that prefix and either equals it or has the challenger suffix). Use the existing GraphQL/REST pattern in that file. Return `[]` on empty match; throw on auth/network errors so the caller can decide how to fail.
3. **Extend** `shared/lib/tend-challenge-gate.ts` with a `detectPairSignals()` helper. The helper takes the PR being evaluated and returns a structured result like `{ pairedViaWorkflowState, pairedViaLinear, pairedViaBranchTwin, errors }`. Each signal is computed independently:
   * **Workflow state**: existing logic via `loadWorkflowStateChallengePairs(repoDir)`.
   * **Linear**: call new helper with the PR's Linear identifier (parsed from PR title or branch); if a sibling open issue exists, set `pairedViaLinear = true`.
   * **Branch twin**: use `git ls-remote origin <twin-branch>` (via `shell-utils.ts` safe exec); if the twin ref exists, set `pairedViaBranchTwin = true`.
4. **Update the gate decision rule.** A PR is gated (held back from merge) if **any** of the three signals is true. Combine signals with logical OR. If the gate holds the PR, log a clear reason indicating which signal(s) fired so the dashboard / logs make the decision auditable.
5. **Implement fail-closed semantics for wavemill PRs.** When Linear or `gh`/`git` lookups error for a wavemill-launched PR (detect via existing wavemill-PR labeling/branch prefix used by the rest of tend), treat the error as "potentially paired" and hold. For non-wavemill PRs (which the gate would not normally pair-gate anyway), preserve current behavior.
6. **Wire it into** `shared/lib/tend-controller.ts`. Update `applyChallengePairGates` (around line 200) to pass `repoDir` plus any Linear/git context already available in the controller scope. Keep the controller thin — all detection logic lives in the gate module.
7. **Add regression tests.** Two new tests reproducing the HOK-1523 timing scenarios (see Section 6 for exact specs). Add them in `shared/lib/tend-controller.test.ts` (preferred — keeps existing fixture/mocking patterns) or in a new `shared/lib/tend-challenge-gate.test.ts` if the controller test file is too entangled to mount the new mocks cleanly. Mock Linear via the same approach already used in the test file; mock `git ls-remote` via `shell-utils` injection.
8. **Run the full validation suite.** Lint, typecheck, run `pnpm test` (or whatever the repo's test runner is — confirm from `package.json`). Verify the existing tend tests still pass.

---

## 4\. Success Criteria

### Functional Requirements

- [ ] **\[REQ-F1\]** Gate holds primary PR when its Linear identifier has an open sibling issue (challenger), even when the challenger task is absent from `workflow-state.json` and the challenger PR is not yet open. The gate's hold reason MUST indicate the Linear sibling signal fired.
- [ ] **\[REQ-F2\]** Gate holds primary PR when a branch-twin exists on `origin` (e.g., `task/foo-challenger` exists when the PR's branch is `task/foo`, or vice versa) but the challenger task is not yet in `workflow-state.json`. Hold reason MUST indicate the branch-twin signal fired.
- [ ] **\[REQ-F3\]** Gate holds primary PR when the challenger task IS registered in `workflow-state.json` but the challenger PR is not yet open. (This covers the case where workflow state is partially populated.)
- [ ] **\[REQ-F4\]** Gate releases primary PR when no pair signal fires AND the comparison run has selected this PR as the winner (or the pair was never created). Behavior matches current gate for unpaired PRs.
- [ ] **\[REQ-F5\]** When the Linear API or `git ls-remote` lookup fails for a wavemill-launched PR, the gate fails closed — holds the PR — and emits a structured log entry so an operator can investigate. Non-wavemill PRs are not pair-gated and behavior remains unchanged.
- [ ] **\[REQ-F6\]** New `listOpenIssuesByIdentifierPrefix(prefix)` helper in `shared/lib/linear.js` returns only issues whose state is open/in-progress (not closed or canceled), and uses the existing Linear client/auth pattern from that file. Returns `[]` for prefix with no matches.

### Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] Gate adds at most one Linear API call and one `git ls-remote` call per PR evaluation (no per-issue iteration). Both calls SHOULD complete within 5 seconds; if they exceed this, the gate logs a warning and holds the PR (fail-closed).
- [ ] No regression in tend evaluation latency for unpaired non-wavemill PRs (no additional API calls in that path).

### Code Quality

- [ ] Follows existing `shared/lib/` thin-tools pattern (business logic in shared lib, not in any tool wrapper)
- [ ] TypeScript types are correct (no `any` unless justified with comment)
- [ ] No lint errors
- [ ] JSDoc on the exported gate function documents the three signal sources and the OR-combined decision rule
- [ ] All existing tend tests remain green

---

## 5\. Implementation Constraints

* **Code style**: Match the surrounding `shared/lib/` style — functional, JSDoc-documented, thin imports, no premature abstraction. New helpers should be small (<100 lines each) and individually testable.
* **Testing**: Use the same mocking style already present in `shared/lib/tend-controller.test.ts` (the most recent merge `eaaec87` modified this file — read it first before adding tests). Do NOT mock `linear.js` if it's already mockable through dependency injection at the controller level. Tests must run as part of the existing `pnpm test` invocation.
* **Security**: Linear API token handling stays within `shared/lib/linear.js` — do not leak it through new return values, error messages, or logs. Branch-twin checks via `git ls-remote` MUST NOT pass user-controlled strings unsanitized to shell — use the parameterized exec helpers in `shared/lib/shell-utils.ts`.
* **Performance**: Cache Linear sibling lookups per tend run if the same identifier prefix appears multiple times (rare, but trivial to memoize). Do not add a per-PR cache that persists across runs.
* **Backwards compatibility**: Workflow-state-driven gate behavior MUST remain a passing signal — this change only ADDS signals, never removes or weakens the existing one. PRs that are currently gated by workflow state must still be gated after this change.
* **Fail-closed on wavemill PRs only**: Non-wavemill PRs (those without the wavemill identifier convention) must not be gated by this new logic — preserve current behavior to avoid unintended side effects on human-authored PRs.
* **No new feature flags**: This is a bug fix; gate the change on correctness, not on a flag. If concerned about rollback, rely on `git revert`.

---

## 6\. Validation Steps

### Functional Requirement Validation

**\[REQ-F1\] Gate holds primary PR when only a Linear sibling exists**

Validation scenario:

1. Setup: Mock `workflow-state.json` to be empty (no challenge pairs). Mock Linear to return one open sibling issue when `listOpenIssuesByIdentifierPrefix('HOK-1523')` is called (e.g., return `[{ identifier: 'HOK-1523_c', state: 'In Progress' }]`). Mock `git ls-remote` to return no twin branch. Open PR is `task/hok-1523-foo` linked to issue `HOK-1523`.
2. Action: Call `applyChallengePairGates` (or the gate function) for the primary PR.
3. Expected result: The PR is in the held/gated set (not the eligible set). The structured hold reason includes `pairedViaLinear: true` and references the sibling identifier `HOK-1523_c`.
4. Edge cases:
   * Sibling issue exists but its state is `Done` / `Canceled` → gate does NOT fire; PR is eligible (only open siblings count)
   * Two open sibling issues exist → gate fires once; hold reason still well-formed (no duplication errors)

**\[REQ-F2\] Gate holds primary PR when only a branch twin exists**

Validation scenario:

1. Setup: Empty `workflow-state.json`. Mock Linear to return `[]`. Mock `git ls-remote origin task/foo-challenger` to return a SHA (twin exists). Open PR's head branch is `task/foo`.
2. Action: Call gate function for the primary PR.
3. Expected result: PR is held; hold reason includes `pairedViaBranchTwin: true` and the twin branch name.
4. Edge cases:
   * PR branch is the challenger (`task/foo-challenger`) and primary `task/foo` exists → gate fires symmetrically (hold either side when twin exists)
   * Twin lookup returns empty stdout → gate does NOT fire on this signal
   * Branch matches but Linear sibling lookup also fires → only one hold entry in the result; no duplicate errors

**\[REQ-F3\] Gate holds primary PR when challenger task is in workflow state but challenger PR is not yet open**

Validation scenario:

1. Setup: `workflow-state.json` contains a challenge pair entry with primary `HOK-1523` and challenger `HOK-1523_c`. No PR exists yet for the challenger. Linear mock can return whatever (signal is satisfied via workflow state). Branch twin can exist or not.
2. Action: Call gate function for the primary PR (which IS open).
3. Expected result: PR is held; hold reason includes `pairedViaWorkflowState: true`. Behavior matches current gate semantics for the workflow-state path.
4. Edge cases:
   * Workflow state lists the pair AND the challenger PR is now open → existing comparison logic decides winner; gate behavior matches pre-change behavior for this case
   * Workflow state malformed (missing fields) → gate logs a warning and falls through to Linear/branch checks

**\[REQ-F4\] Gate releases unpaired primary PR**

Validation scenario:

1. Setup: Empty `workflow-state.json`. Mock Linear to return `[]`. Mock `git ls-remote` to return no twin. Single PR `task/foo` linked to issue `HOK-1600`.
2. Action: Call gate function.
3. Expected result: PR is in the eligible-to-merge set. No hold reason emitted.
4. Edge cases:
   * PR has no Linear identifier (manual / human PR without the wavemill convention) → not pair-gated (current behavior preserved)
   * PR's branch starts with `task/` but has no `_challenger` twin on origin → eligible

**\[REQ-F5\] Gate fails closed on Linear / git errors for wavemill PRs**

Validation scenario:

1. Setup: Empty `workflow-state.json`. Mock Linear to throw a network error. Wavemill-launched PR.
2. Action: Call gate function.
3. Expected result: PR is held with a structured error reason indicating the Linear lookup failed. A warning is logged. PR is NOT in the eligible set.
4. Edge cases:
   * `git ls-remote` exits non-zero → same fail-closed behavior; PR held
   * Both Linear and git fail → still held, with both errors recorded
   * Non-wavemill PR encounters Linear/git errors → existing behavior preserved (not pair-gated)

**\[REQ-F6\]** `listOpenIssuesByIdentifierPrefix` filters by open state and returns empty array for unknown prefixes

Validation scenario:

1. Setup: Use the existing Linear test mock pattern. Seed two issues: `HOK-1523_c` (Open) and `HOK-1523_old` (Done).
2. Action: Call `listOpenIssuesByIdentifierPrefix('HOK-1523')`.
3. Expected result: Returns one issue (`HOK-1523_c`). The Done issue is filtered out.
4. Edge cases:
   * Prefix with zero matches → returns `[]`
   * Auth/network error → throws (caller decides to fail closed)
   * Prefix string contains characters that need escaping in the Linear query → still produces correct filter (test with a safe known prefix)

---

### Input/Output Verification

**Valid Inputs:**

* PR with workflow-state pair, no Linear sibling, no twin → Held (workflow-state signal)
* PR with no workflow-state pair, Linear sibling exists, no twin → Held (Linear signal)
* PR with no workflow-state pair, no Linear sibling, twin branch exists → Held (branch signal)
* PR with no signals firing → Eligible

**Invalid Inputs:**

* Linear API throws on lookup (wavemill PR) → Held with `errors.linear` populated
* `git ls-remote` exits 1 (wavemill PR) → Held with `errors.git` populated
* PR with malformed Linear identifier → Skip Linear lookup, log warning, fall through to branch check

---

### Standard Validation Commands

```bash
# 1. Lint passes
pnpm lint
# Expected: no errors

# 2. Type check passes
pnpm typecheck
# Expected: no type errors (confirm script name from package.json — may be tsc --noEmit)

# 3. Tests pass — entire repo
pnpm test
# Expected: all tests pass, including new tend-challenge-gate / tend-controller tests

# 4. Run only tend-controller tests during development for fast iteration
pnpm test shared/lib/tend-controller.test.ts
# Expected: all green
```

---

### Manual Verification Checklist

- [ ] Replay HOK-1523 timing in a tmp repo with mocked Linear and `gh`: open primary PR, withhold challenger registration for 60+ seconds, verify gate holds primary the entire time
- [ ] Verify a single-task (non-paired) PR still merges promptly with no extra latency vs. pre-change
- [ ] Confirm gate hold reasons are visible in tend's existing log output (grep for the new structured fields)
- [ ] Confirm no new `any` types or `// @ts-ignore` introduced in the diff
- [ ] Spot-check that `listOpenIssuesByIdentifierPrefix` follows the Linear client patterns already in `shared/lib/linear.js` (auth, error shape, return types)

---

## 7\. Definition of Done

- [ ] All success criteria met
- [ ] All validation steps pass with specific, measurable outcomes
- [ ] Each functional requirement has at least one concrete validation scenario (Section 6)
- [ ] Edge cases (Linear errors, git errors, missing identifiers, closed sibling issues) are documented and tested
- [ ] No unrelated changes included (fixture cleanup is a separate task — do NOT touch the 11 migration fixtures)
- [ ] Commit message references HOK-1544
- [ ] PR created with clear description summarizing the three signals and the fail-closed semantics

---

## 8\. Rollback Plan

* **Revert**: `git revert <merge-sha>` — the change is contained to `shared/lib/tend-challenge-gate.ts`, `shared/lib/tend-controller.ts`, `shared/lib/linear.js`, and the test files. No state migrations are introduced, so revert is clean.
* **Operational mitigation if revert is delayed**: Operators can manually pause the tend controller (existing pause mechanism) while the bad version is in production; this is the same mitigation that would apply for any tend-controller bug.
* **No data migration**: This change reads from existing sources (workflow-state.json, Linear API, git origin); it writes nothing new to disk.
* **No feature flag**: As stated in Section 5, no flag — rollback via revert.

---

## 9\. Release Readiness

* **database_change_risk**: none
* **env_changes**: none
* **config_changes**: none
* **manual_steps**: none

---

## 10\. Proposed Labels

**Risk Level**: `Risk: Medium`

**Justification**: Touches the merge-eligibility decision path for the autonomous tend controller, which has direct effect on what code reaches `auto/integration` and `main`. Not "High" because there are no schema changes, no auth/infra changes, and the change only ADDS gate signals (preserves existing workflow-state-driven behavior). Failure mode of the change is over-holding (delays a merge), not under-holding, which is the safer side.

---

* `shared/lib/tend-challenge-gate.ts`
* `shared/lib/tend-controller.ts`
* `shared/lib/linear.js`
* `shared/lib/tend-controller.test.ts`
* `shared/lib/tend-challenge-gate.test.ts` (only if added)

**Label**: `Files: tend-challenge-gate.ts, tend-controller.ts, linear.js, tend-controller.test.ts`

**Purpose**: Prevents parallel tasks from modifying the same files, especially `tend-controller.ts` which was just touched by `eaaec87` (promote checks fix).

---

**Architectural Layer**: `Layer: Service`

**Purpose**: Pure shared-lib business logic; no UI, API route, DB schema, or infra changes.

---

**Area**: `Area: Tend`

**Purpose**: Avoid running 2+ tasks affecting the tend controller / challenge-gate area concurrently. Recent activity in `tend-controller.ts` (commit `eaaec87`, `650c863`) indicates this area is hot — sequential work avoids merge conflicts.

---

**Test Coverage**: `Tests: Unit`

**Purpose**: New tests are unit-level (mocked Linear, mocked git, mocked workflow-state). No E2E or integration test overhead.

---

**Component**: `Component: TendChallengeGate`

**Purpose**: Avoid running 2+ tasks modifying the challenge gate at the same time.

---

### Label Summary

```
Suggested labels for this task:
- Risk: Medium
- Files: shared/lib/tend-challenge-gate.ts, shared/lib/tend-controller.ts, shared/lib/linear.js, shared/lib/tend-controller.test.ts
```

**How these labels help the autonomous workflow:**

* **Risk: Medium** — Max 2 Medium risk tasks can run in parallel
* **Files: ...** — Prevents conflicts with any other task touching the tend controller or Linear client (e.g., the recent promote checks fix)
* **Layer: Service** — Can run in parallel with UI / DB / Infra tasks
* **Area: Tend** — Prevents conflicts with other tend-area work

# HOK-1525: Routing / challenge mode conflicts

# Routing / Challenge Mode Conflicts - Quick Reference

**Issue ID**: HOK-1525

## Objective

Fix challenge mode task selection in `shared/lib/wavemill-mill.sh` so that the call to `resolve-challenge-task.ts` passes the `--file` argument, enabling workflow-aware (stage-aware) task routing for challenger/Codex paths. Without this, challenger selection silently falls back to non-routed selection, weakening Codex challenger quality and producing routing/challenge mode conflicts.

## Key Files

* `shared/lib/wavemill-mill.sh` (\~line 1699: challenge selection invocation)
* `tools/resolve-challenge-task.ts` (consumer of `--file`)
* `shared/lib/stage-aware-router.ts` (workflow-aware routing)
* `shared/lib/workflow-router.ts` (operating-mode + routing decisions)
* `tests/` (new shell-level test fixture for challenge selection invocation)

## Critical Constraints

1. Do NOT change the public CLI surface of `resolve-challenge-task.ts` beyond ensuring `--file` is honored; preserve backward compatibility for existing callers.
2. The fix MUST resolve the actual task packet file path used by the worktree (the same path the primary selection passes), not a guess. Reuse the existing variable holding the task packet file in `wavemill-mill.sh` rather than reconstructing it.
3. Routing must continue to respect operating mode — when constrained/survival, challenge selection must still skip LLM-based difficulty classification per `router.md`.

## Success Criteria (High-Level)

- [ ] `resolve-challenge-task.ts` receives `--file <task-packet-path>` from the challenge selection call site at `shared/lib/wavemill-mill.sh:~1699`
- [ ] Challenger selection routes through workflow-aware logic (stage-aware-router) when a file is provided, with measurable behavior parity to primary selection
- [ ] Existing primary selection behavior is unchanged (no regressions in `wavemill-mill.sh` primary path)
- [ ] New shell test asserts the invocation includes `--file` and points at a real file
- [ ] `bash tests/check-shell.sh` and existing TypeScript tests pass; PR opened referencing HOK-1525

## Detailed Sections

Full details available on-demand in [task-packet-details.md](<http://task-packet-details.md>):

* [Section 1: Complete Objective & Scope](<#1-objective>)
* [Section 2: Technical Context](<#2-technical-context>)
* [Section 3: Implementation Approach](<#3-implementation-approach>)
* [Section 4: Success Criteria](<#4-success-criteria>)
* [Section 5: Implementation Constraints](<#5-implementation-constraints>)
* [Section 6: Validation Steps](<#6-validation-steps>)
* [Section 7: Definition of Done](<#7-definition-of-done>)
* [Section 8: Rollback Plan](<#8-rollback-plan>)
* [Section 9: Release Readiness](<#9-release-readiness>)
* [Section 10: Proposed Labels](<#10-proposed-labels>)

**Implementation Note**: Start with this overview. Read detailed sections on-demand as you implement.

---

## 1\. Objective

### What

Pass the `--file <task-packet-path>` argument from the challenge-mode task-selection call site in `shared/lib/wavemill-mill.sh` (around line 1699) to `tools/resolve-challenge-task.ts` so that challenge mode performs the same workflow-aware (stage-aware) task routing that the primary selection performs.

### Why

Challenge mode currently invokes `resolve-challenge-task.ts` without `--file`, which means the challenger/Codex pathway cannot consult the task packet to make a workflow-aware routing decision. This degrades the quality of challenger model selection (a likely contributor to "only Claude" challenger behavior) and creates a quiet divergence between primary-selection and challenge-selection routing. Restoring `--file` makes the two paths symmetric and lets the operating-mode-aware router (per `.wavemill/context/router.md`) drive challenge selection too.

### Scope In

* Update the challenge-selection invocation in `shared/lib/wavemill-mill.sh` near line 1699 to pass `--file <task-packet-path>`.
* Verify that `tools/resolve-challenge-task.ts` already accepts `--file` and routes through workflow-aware logic; if it does not, add minimal support for `--file` consistent with the primary `resolve-task.ts` / `stage-aware-router` patterns.
* Add a focused shell test under `tests/` that asserts the challenge-selection call site invokes the resolver with `--file` pointing at the expected task packet file.
* Confirm existing routing operating-mode behavior (constrained/survival) is preserved for the challenge path.

### Scope Out

* Any change to `resolve-task.ts` (primary selection) behavior.
* Any change to model registry classes, routing ladders, or operating-mode derivation logic.
* Any new product features in challenger workflows beyond passing `--file`.
* Refactoring `wavemill-mill.sh` beyond the minimal call-site fix and any small adjacent cleanup needed to source the file path safely.
* Documentation rewrites of `router.md` or `eval-system.md` (auto-update is allowed via post-merge hook only).

---

## 2\. Technical Context

### Repository

This work happens entirely in the `wavemill` repo (current working directory). No cross-repo changes.

### Key Files

* `shared/lib/wavemill-mill.sh` — challenge selection call site (\~line 1699). The shell driver that invokes `tools/resolve-challenge-task.ts` for challenger/Codex selection.
* `tools/resolve-challenge-task.ts` — TypeScript resolver invoked by the shell. Must accept `--file ` and feed it into the workflow-aware router.
* `shared/lib/stage-aware-router.ts` — KNN-based workflow-aware routing fallback used by both primary and challenge resolvers.
* `shared/lib/workflow-router.ts` — Authoritative routing entry point that respects operating mode and `modelsAvailable`.
* `shared/lib/operating-mode.ts` — Source of `getCurrentOperatingMode()` used by routing to switch between normal/constrained/survival.
* `tools/resolve-task.ts` — Reference implementation for primary selection; mirror its `--file` handling.
* `tests/check-shell.sh` — Shell test harness used by the repo (per [CLAUDE.md](<http://CLAUDE.md>) and recent commits).
* A new `tests/fixtures/...` shell fixture or `tests/wavemill-mill-challenge.test.sh` to assert the call-site change.

### Relevant Subsystem Specs

* **Router** (`.wavemill/context/router.md`)
  * **Key Constraints**: Always prepend degraded-mode rationale to routing decisions when constrained or survival; treat constrained/survival as aggregate-across-frontier states; respect `modelsAvailable` option for test injection; skip LLM-based difficulty classification in constrained/survival modes.
  * **Known Failure Modes**: Degraded routing falls back to full pool when restricted-class models are missing; `constrained` mode can fire incorrectly if operating mode is derived from a single-model check rather than aggregating frontier IDs.
  * **Testing Patterns**: `shared/lib/workflow-router.test.ts` uses `writeQuotaState` helpers to inject quota state; tests cover survival/constrained/normal modes.
* **Eval System** (`.wavemill/context/eval-system.md`)
  * **Key Constraints**: Schema evolution must be additive; don't break readers of `.wavemill/evals/evals.jsonl`. This task should not modify schemas, but routing decisions emitted along the challenge path must continue to flow through the eval pipeline unchanged.
  * **Known Failure Modes**: New fields without JSON schema updates fail validation; missing `logFallbackEvents` skips fallback eval rows.
  * **Testing Patterns**: Use temp repos for `llm-cli` fallback telemetry assertions if any eval-emitting paths are touched (this task should avoid touching them).
* **Quota Tracking** (`.wavemill/context/quota-tracking.md`)
  * **Key Constraints**: Quota state drives operating mode; routing must reserve premium capacity in constrained/survival.
  * **Known Failure Modes**: Manual override precedence and expiration behavior must be preserved.
  * **Testing Patterns**: Use `writeQuotaState` test helpers when validating challenge-mode routing under constrained mode.

### Dependencies

* No new npm dependencies expected.
* Depends on existing `shared/lib/state-mutex.ts` patterns only if state writes are touched (they should not be in this fix).
* Depends on `bash`, `jq` (already required by wavemill scripts) for the new shell test.

### Architecture Notes

* `shared/lib/wavemill-mill.sh` is a shell driver. Per [CLAUDE.md](<http://CLAUDE.md>), business logic should live in `shared/lib/*.ts` and tools are thin wrappers; the shell should call the TypeScript tool with the right arguments rather than re-implementing routing logic.
* Per `router.md`, routing decisions must respect operating mode and aggregate-across-frontier semantics. Passing `--file` does not change that — it just gives the resolver access to the workflow's task packet so the stage-aware router can score against the actual content.
* Mirror the primary-selection invocation as closely as possible. If primary uses `npx tsx tools/resolve-task.ts --file "$TASK_PACKET_PATH" ...`, challenge selection should use the analogous form against `tools/resolve-challenge-task.ts`.
* Resolve the task packet file path by reusing the existing variable that primary selection uses in the same shell function (do not re-derive it from session state).

---

## 3\. Implementation Approach

1. **Locate the call site.** Open `shared/lib/wavemill-mill.sh` at line 1699 and identify the function and surrounding variables. Confirm which variable already holds the task packet path used by primary selection in the same code region.
2. **Audit** `tools/resolve-challenge-task.ts`. Verify that it already accepts `--file ` and forwards the file content/path to `stage-aware-router.ts` / `workflow-router.ts`. If `--file` is missing or unwired, add minimal support that mirrors `tools/resolve-task.ts`. Do not introduce new flags beyond what primary selection uses.
3. **Update the shell invocation.** Change the challenge-selection call near line 1699 to pass `--file "$TASK_PACKET_PATH"` (or the existing equivalent variable name found in step 1). Quote the path defensively to handle spaces.
4. **Preserve operating-mode handling.** Do not pass any flag that would force LLM-based difficulty classification when in constrained/survival mode. Let `workflow-router.ts` handle the operating-mode branching as documented in `.wavemill/context/router.md`.
5. **Mirror primary-selection environment.** Confirm any environment variables exported for primary selection (e.g., quota-state path, repo dir) are also exported for the challenge invocation. If not, add them.
6. **Write a shell test.** Create `tests/wavemill-mill-challenge.test.sh` (or extend the closest existing test, e.g., near `tests/wavemill-expand-direct.test.sh`) that:
   * Stubs `tools/resolve-challenge-task.ts` (e.g., via PATH shim or by replacing with a recorder that prints its argv).
   * Invokes the relevant function from `shared/lib/wavemill-mill.sh` with a fixture task packet.
   * Asserts the recorded argv contains `--file` and that the value matches the fixture path.
7. **Add (if absent) a TypeScript-level assertion.** If `tools/resolve-challenge-task.ts` lacked `--file` support and you added it, add a minimal unit test alongside it (mirroring `tools/resolve-task.ts` tests, if any) verifying that `--file` is parsed and forwarded to the router.
8. **Run validation.** Run `bash tests/check-shell.sh`, the new shell test, and the relevant TypeScript test suite (`shared/lib/workflow-router.test.ts`). Confirm no regressions.
9. **Open PR.** PR title `fix: Pass --file to resolve-challenge-task for workflow-aware routing`, body referencing HOK-1525 and explaining the symmetry restoration with primary selection.

## 4\. Success Criteria

### Functional Requirements

- [ ] **\[REQ-F1\]** The challenge-selection call site in `shared/lib/wavemill-mill.sh` (currently around line 1699) invokes `tools/resolve-challenge-task.ts` with `--file <task-packet-path>` where `<task-packet-path>` is the same path used by primary selection in the surrounding context.

* **Code style (TypeScript):** If editing `tools/resolve-challenge-task.ts`, keep the tool thin and delegate to `shared/lib/`. Use `runTool` pattern if it is already in use there; otherwise match the surrounding style.
* **Routing semantics:** Do not bypass `workflow-router.ts` operating-mode logic. The fix must not introduce a branch that forces LLM-based classification in constrained/survival modes.

# HOK-1544: Tend challenge gate has a registration race; primary can merge before challenger is registered

# Tend Challenge Gate Registration Race - Quick Reference

**Issue ID**: HOK-1544

## Objective

Fix the registration race in tend's challenge gate that allows the primary PR of a challenge pair to merge into `auto/integration` before the challenger task is registered in workflow state. Add a Linear-backed cross-check (Plan A) so the gate can recognize in-flight pair members independent of `workflow-state.json`, with a branch-name heuristic (Plan B) as a fallback for when Linear is unavailable.

## Key Files

* `shared/lib/tend-challenge-gate.ts`
* `shared/lib/tend-controller.ts`
* `shared/lib/linear.js`
* `shared/lib/tend-controller.test.ts`
* `shared/lib/tend-challenge-gate.test.ts`

## Critical Constraints

1. The gate MUST hold a primary PR when *any* signal — workflow state, Linear sibling issue, or branch-name twin — implies a challenger exists, even if the challenger PR is not yet open.
2. Linear and gh lookups MUST fail closed: if the lookup errors or times out for a wavemill-launched PR, the gate holds the PR rather than letting it through (avoids re-introducing the race silently).
3. Existing tend behavior for non-paired PRs (single-task PRs with no challenger sibling) MUST remain unchanged — no extra latency, no spurious holds.

## Success Criteria (High-Level)

- [ ] Gate holds primary PR when challenger task is in workflow state but challenger PR is not yet open
- [ ] Gate holds primary PR when only a Linear sibling issue (challenger identifier) exists, not yet in workflow state
- [ ] Gate holds primary PR when only a `task/<slug>-challenger` (or twin) branch exists on origin
- [ ] All existing `tend-controller` tests remain green; new regression test reproduces HOK-1523 timing
- [ ] PR created and linked to HOK-1544

## Detailed Sections

Full details available on-demand in [task-packet-details.md](<http://task-packet-details.md>):

* [Section 1: Complete Objective & Scope](<#1-objective>)
* [Section 2: Technical Context](<#2-technical-context>)
* [Section 3: Implementation Approach](<#3-implementation-approach>)
* [Section 4: Success Criteria](<#4-success-criteria>)
* [Section 5: Implementation Constraints](<#5-implementation-constraints>)
* [Section 6: Validation Steps](<#6-validation-steps>)
* [Section 7: Definition of Done](<#7-definition-of-done>)
* [Section 8: Rollback Plan](<#8-rollback-plan>)
* [Section 9: Release Readiness](<#9-release-readiness>)
* [Section 10: Proposed Labels](<#10-proposed-labels>)

**Implementation Note**: Start with this overview. Read detailed sections on-demand as you implement.

---

## 1\. Objective

### What

Close the registration race in `shared/lib/tend-challenge-gate.ts` so that the primary PR of a challenge pair cannot be merged into `auto/integration` while the challenger task is still in the process of registering. Add Linear-based and branch-name-based detection so the gate has authoritative pair information even when `workflow-state.json` is incomplete.

### Why

On 2026-05-04 (incident HOK-1523), PR #497 (primary) merged into `auto/integration` at 19:02:24, then 16 minutes later the challenge comparison ran and selected challenger #501 as the winner — but #497 was already merged. Both PRs ended up in `auto/integration` and queued for promotion to `main`, breaking the "only one side wins" guarantee of the challenge system. Significant code overlap (in `shared/lib/migration-ast.ts`, `shared/lib/ready-stage.ts`) plus 11 dead test fixtures from the loser would pollute `main`. 2. **Add** `listOpenIssuesByIdentifierPrefix()` to `shared/lib/linear.js`. Accepts a Linear identifier (e.g., `HOK-1523`) and returns all open Linear issues whose identifier matches the pair convention used by wavemill (e.g., starts with that prefix and either equals it or has the challenger suffix). Use the existing GraphQL/REST pattern in that file. Return `[]` on empty match; throw on auth/network errors so the caller can decide how to fail.
3. **Extend** `shared/lib/tend-challenge-gate.ts` with a `detectPairSignals()` helper. The helper takes the PR being evaluated and returns a structured result like `{ pairedViaWorkflowState, pairedViaLinear, pairedViaBranchTwin, errors }`. Each signal is computed independently:
   * **Workflow state**: existing logic via `loadWorkflowStateChallengePairs(repoDir)`.
   * **Linear**: call new helper with the PR's Linear identifier (parsed from PR title or branch); if a sibling open issue exists, set `pairedViaLinear = true`.

4. **Update the gate decision rule.** A PR is gated (held back from merge) if **any** of the three signals is true. Combine signals with logical OR. If the gate holds the PR, log a clear reason indicating which signal(s) fired so the dashboard / logs make the decision auditable.
5. **Implement fail-closed semantics for wavemill PRs.** When Linear or `gh`/`git` lookups error for a wavemill-launched PR (detect via existing wavemill-PR labeling/branch prefix used by the rest of tend), treat the error as "potentially paired" and hold. ## 4\. Success Criteria

### Functional Requirements

- [ ] **\[REQ-F1\]** Gate holds primary PR when its Linear identifier has an open sibling issue (challenger), even when the challenger task is absent from `workflow-state.json` and the challenger PR is not yet open. The gate's hold reason MUST indicate the Linear sibling signal fired.
- [ ] **\[REQ-F2\]** Gate holds primary PR when a branch-twin exists on `origin` (e.g., `task/foo-challenger` exists when the PR's branch is `task/foo`, or vice versa) but the challenger task is not yet in `workflow-state.json`. Hold reason MUST indicate the branch-twin signal fired.
- [ ] **\[REQ-F3\]** Gate holds primary PR when the challenger task IS registered in `workflow-state.json` but the challenger PR is not yet open. (This covers the case where workflow state is partially populated.)
- [ ] **\[REQ-F4\]** Gate releases primary PR when no pair signal fires AND the comparison run has selected this PR as the winner (or the pair was never created). Behavior matches current gate for unpaired PRs.
- [ ] **\[REQ-F5\]** When the Linear API or `git ls-remote` lookup fails for a wavemill-launched PR, the gate fails closed — holds the PR — and emits a structured log entry so an operator can investigate. Non-wavemill PRs are not pair-gated and behavior remains unchanged.
- [ ] **\[REQ-F6\]** New `listOpenIssuesByIdentifierPrefix(prefix)` helper in `shared/lib/linear.js` returns only issues whose state is open/in-progress (not closed or canceled), and uses the existing Linear client/auth pattern from that file. Returns `[]` for prefix with no matches.

### Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] Gate adds at most one Linear API call and one `git ls-remote` call per PR evaluation (no per-issue iteration). Both calls SHOULD complete within 5 seconds; if they exceed this, the gate logs a warning and holds the PR (fail-closed).
- [ ] No regression in tend evaluation latency for unpaired non-wavemill PRs (no additional API calls in that path).

## 6\. Validation Steps

### Functional Requirement Validation

**\[REQ-F1\] Gate holds primary PR when only a Linear sibling exists**

Validation scenario:

1. Setup: Mock `workflow-state.json` to be empty (no challenge pairs). Mock Linear to return one open sibling issue when `listOpenIssuesByIdentifierPrefix('HOK-1523')` is called (e.g., return `[{ identifier: 'HOK-1523_c', state: 'In Progress' }]`). Mock `git ls-remote` to return no twin branch. Open PR is `task/hok-1523-foo` linked to issue `HOK-1523`.
2. Action: Call `applyChallengePairGates` (or the gate function) for the primary PR.
3. Expected result: The PR is in the held/gated set (not the eligible set). The structured hold reason includes `pairedViaLinear: true` and references the sibling identifier `HOK-1523_c`.
4. Edge cases:
   * Sibling issue exists but its state is `Done` / `Canceled` → gate does NOT fire; PR is eligible (only open siblings count)
   * Two open sibling issues exist → gate fires once; hold reason still well-formed (no duplication errors)

**\[REQ-F2\] Gate holds primary PR when only a branch twin exists**

Validation scenario:

1. Setup: Empty `workflow-state.json`. Mock Linear to return `[]`. Mock `git ls-remote origin task/foo-challenger` to return a SHA (twin exists). Open PR's head branch is `task/foo`.
2. Action: Call gate function for the primary PR.
3. Expected result: PR is held; hold reason includes `pairedViaBranchTwin: true` and the twin branch name.
4. Edge cases:
   * PR branch is the challenger (`task/foo-challenger`) and primary `task/foo` exists → gate fires symmetrically (hold either side when twin exists)
   * Twin lookup returns empty stdout → gate does NOT fire on this signal
   * Branch matches but Linear sibling lookup also fires → only one hold entry in the result; no duplicate errors

**\[REQ-F3\] Gate holds primary PR when challenger task is in workflow state but challenger PR is not yet open**

Validation scenario:

1. Setup: `workflow-state.json` contains a challenge pair entry with primary `HOK-1523` and challenger `HOK-1523_c`. No PR exists yet for the challenger. Linear mock can return whatever (signal is satisfied via workflow state). Branch twin can exist or not.
2. Action: Call gate function for the primary PR (which IS open).
3. Expected result: PR is held; hold reason includes `pairedViaWorkflowState: true`. Behavior matches current gate semantics for the workflow-state path.
4. Edge cases:
   * Workflow state lists the pair AND the challenger PR is now open → existing comparison logic decides winner; gate behavior matches pre-change behavior for this case
   * Workflow state malformed (missing fields) → gate logs a warning and falls through to Linear/branch checks

**\[REQ-F4\] Gate releases unpaired primary PR**

Validation scenario:

1. Setup: Empty `workflow-state.json`. Mock Linear to return `[]`. Mock `git ls-remote` to return no twin. Single PR `task/foo` linked to issue `HOK-1600`.
2. Action: Call gate function.
3. Expected result: PR is in the eligible-to-merge set. No hold reason emitted.
4. Edge cases:
   * PR has no Linear identifier (manual / human PR without the wavemill convention) → not pair-gated (current behavior preserved)
   * PR's branch starts with `task/` but has no `_challenger` twin on origin → eligible

**\[REQ-F5\] Gate fails closed on Linear / git errors for wavemill PRs**

Validation scenario:

1. Setup: Empty `workflow-state.json`. Mock Linear to throw a network error. Wavemill-launched PR.
2. Action: Call gate function.
3. Expected result: PR is held with a structured error reason indicating the Linear lookup failed. A warning is logged. PR is NOT in the eligible set.
4. Edge cases:
   * `git ls-remote` exits non-zero → same fail-closed behavior; PR held
   * Both Linear and git fail → still held, with both errors recorded
   * Non-wavemill PR encounters Linear/git errors → existing behavior preserved (not pair-gated)

**\[REQ-F6\]** `listOpenIssuesByIdentifierPrefix` filters by open state and returns empty array for unknown prefixes

Validation scenario:

1. Setup: Use the existing Linear test mock pattern. Seed two issues: `HOK-1523_c` (Open) and `HOK-1523_old` (Done).
2. Action: Call `listOpenIssuesByIdentifierPrefix('HOK-1523')`.
3. Expected result: Returns one issue (`HOK-1523_c`). The Done issue is filtered out.
4. Edge cases:
   * Prefix with zero matches → returns `[]`
   * Auth/network error → throws (caller decides to fail closed)
   * Prefix string contains characters that need escaping in the Linear query → still produces correct filter (test with a safe known prefix)

# HOK-1545: Add wavemill mill --dry-run end-to-end harness for startup integration coverage

# Add wavemill mill --dry-run end-to-end harness for startup integration coverage - Quick Reference

**Issue ID**: HOK-1545

## Objective

Add a `--dry-run` mode to `wavemill mill` that exercises the full startup pipeline (launch plan construction, route resolution, jq filter evaluation) against fixture data with stubbed agents/Linear/gh/tmux, plus a lifecycle fixture that runs it in CI. This catches a class of merge-induced regressions (jq filter syntax errors, missing variables, field-shape mismatches between mill and startup-runner) that today's isolated unit tests miss.

## Key Files

* `wavemill` (top-level launcher) — add `--dry-run` flag parsing
* `shared/lib/wavemill-mill.sh` — gate Linear/GitHub calls behind `WAVEMILL_DRY_RUN`; emit launch plan to configurable path
* `shared/lib/wavemill-startup-runner.sh` — gate tmux session creation and `agent_launch_*` calls behind `WAVEMILL_DRY_RUN`
* `tests/fixtures/lifecycle/mill_dry_run_full_pipeline.sh` — NEW fixture exercising the full pipeline
* `tests/fixtures/lifecycle/tend-fixture-lib.sh` — extend with `write_fake_linear` helper alongside existing `write_fake_gh`/`write_fake_git`
* `tests/check-shell.sh` — register the new fixture under "Startup Lifecycle Fixtures"

## Critical Constraints

1. **No network calls in dry-run mode** — all Linear, GitHub (`gh`), git remote, and tmux interactions must be routed through fixture stubs; CI must pass with no network access
2. **Real construction code paths must execute** — `build_launch_plan` and the jq filters that build `route_payload`, `tasks_json`, etc. in `wavemill-mill.sh` must run unmodified; only their I/O sinks (Linear writes, tmux spawning, agent launching) may be stubbed
3. **Fixture runtime budget < 30s** — must fit inside the existing Lifecycle Integration Tests GitHub Actions job without inflating CI time

## Success Criteria (High-Level)

- [ ] `wavemill mill --dry-run` against fixture backlog produces a valid `launch-plan.json` and exits 0
- [ ] Manually breaking any of the `route_payload` / `tasks_json` / launch-plan jq filters causes the new fixture to fail
- [ ] Fixture makes zero real network calls (verified by absence of stubs being bypassed)
- [ ] New fixture registered in `tests/check-shell.sh` and runs as part of Lifecycle Integration Tests
- [ ] Total fixture runtime < 30s
- [ ] Tests and lint pass; PR created and linked

## Detailed Sections

Full details available on-demand in [task-packet-details.md](<http://task-packet-details.md>):

* [Section 1: Complete Objective & Scope](<#1-objective>)
* [Section 2: Technical Context](<#2-technical-context>)

* [Section 9: Rollback Plan](<#9-rollback-plan>)
