# HOK-1622: Remove old jobs from Background jobs

# Remove old jobs from Background jobs - Quick Reference

**Issue ID**: HOK-1622

## Objective

The wavemill background jobs section accumulates old job records indefinitely, creating a never-ending log instead of showing only currently-relevant session jobs. Implement cleanup of stale/completed background jobs at session start and session end so the jobs view reflects only the current session's running and recently-completed work.

## Key Files

* `shared/lib/job-tracker.ts`
* `shared/lib/wavemill-mill.sh`
* `shared/lib/wavemill-startup-runner.sh`
* `shared/lib/wavemill-status.sh`
* `shared/lib/wavemill-common.sh`

## Critical Constraints

1. All mutations to `.wavemill/state/monitored-jobs.json` (or equivalent) MUST go through `state_mutate`/`mutateJsonState` — never read-modify-write directly.
2. Cleanup must NEVER remove jobs that are still `running` (alive PID) or whose side effects have not yet been reaped (`evalCompleted`/`challengeCompared` flags must be honored before deletion).
3. Backward compatibility: existing job state files without new fields (e.g., `sessionId`) must continue to parse — additive schema only.

## Success Criteria (High-Level)

- [ ] On session startup, jobs from prior sessions (and any completed/timed-out/failed jobs whose side effects have been applied) are removed from the persisted job state before the dashboard renders.
- [ ] On session end (clean shutdown), completed/failed jobs are purged so a stopped session leaves no dangling job entries.
- [ ] The Background jobs dashboard section only shows jobs from the current session (running, plus recently-completed within the session).
- [ ] Tests cover startup cleanup, shutdown cleanup, and the invariant that `running` and unreaped jobs are preserved.
- [ ] Tests and lint pass; PR created and linked.

## Detailed Sections

Full details available on-demand in task-packet-details.md:

* [Section 1: Complete Objective & Scope](<#1-objective>)
* [Section 2: Technical Context](<#2-technical-context>)
* [Section 3: Implementation Approach](<#3-implementation-approach>)
* [Section 4: Success Criteria](<#4-success-criteria>)
* [Section 5: Implementation Constraints](<#5-implementation-constraints>)
* [Section 6: Validation Steps](<#6-validation-steps>)
* [Section 8: Definition of Done](<#8-definition-of-done>)
* [Section 9: Rollback Plan](<#9-rollback-plan>)
* [Section 10: Release Readiness](<#10-release-readiness>)
* [Section 11: Proposed Labels](<#11-proposed-labels>)

**Implementation Note**: Start with this overview. Read detailed sections on-demand as you implement.

---

## 1\. Objective

### What

Implement session-scoped cleanup of background job records in wavemill so the "Background jobs" dashboard section only displays jobs relevant to the current session, by purging stale/completed jobs at session startup and at session shutdown.

### Why

The background jobs view (eval, comparison, post-merge, etc.) currently behaves as an append-only log: every job that has ever run accumulates in the persisted state file (`.wavemill/state/monitored-jobs.json`) and is rendered forever. This creates visual noise, hides what's actually running now, slows the status renderer as the array grows, and makes the dashboard misleading after long-lived repos. Operators cannot trust the jobs section as a "what is happening right now?" indicator.

### Scope In

* Identify the canonical job-state file used by the monitor loop (job-tracker / monitored-jobs).
* Add cleanup logic that runs **at session startup** (before the dashboard first renders) to drop jobs not belonging to the current session and any already-reaped completed jobs.
* Add cleanup logic that runs **at session end / clean shutdown** to drop completed/failed/timed-out jobs whose side effects have been applied.
* Annotate new job records with a `sessionId` (current `WAVEMILL_SESSION`) when they are launched, so cleanup can distinguish current-session jobs from prior-session leftovers.
* Tolerant parsing for legacy records missing `sessionId` — these are treated as "not in current session" and eligible for cleanup at startup (they cannot have a live PID belonging to this session).
* Tests covering startup cleanup, shutdown cleanup, the running-job preservation invariant, and the unreaped-side-effect preservation invariant.

### Scope Out

* No change to the visual layout of the Background jobs section beyond it now being shorter (no new columns, no new headings).
* No change to job *launch* semantics or the spawn/poll/settle lifecycle (HOK-1564 contract preserved).
* No change to JSONL eval persistence (`.wavemill/evals/evals.jsonl`) — that's an append-only training log and is intentionally not session-scoped.
* No change to the result file / exit sentinel pattern.
* No retroactive backfill of `sessionId` on legacy in-flight jobs — they will be cleaned at next startup as designed.
* No new config knobs in this PR (cleanup is unconditional). Could be added in a follow-up if operators want retention windows.

---

## 2\. Technical Context

### Repository

`wavemill` (this repo). Single-repo change.

### Key Files

* `shared/lib/job-tracker.ts` — Job lifecycle (launch, poll, settle, list). Will gain a `cleanupStaleJobs()` / `purgeCompletedJobs()` helper and `sessionId` recorded on launch.
* `shared/lib/wavemill-mill.sh` — Monitor loop entry point. Will invoke startup cleanup before the first poll, and shutdown cleanup on clean exit.
* `shared/lib/wavemill-startup-runner.sh` — Session startup. Best place to call cleanup before dashboard renders for the first time.
* `shared/lib/wavemill-status.sh` — Reads job state to render the Background jobs section. May need a tolerant filter so legacy records without `sessionId` don't render as "current".
* `shared/lib/wavemill-common.sh` — Shell helpers; may host a `purge_old_jobs()` shell wrapper that delegates to a TS helper.
* `.wavemill/state/monitored-jobs.json` — Persisted job-state file (existing). Schema is extended additively with `sessionId`.

### Relevant Subsystem Specs

* **Manager** (`.wavemill/context/manager.md`)
  * **Key Constraints**: Use `state_mutate` (shell) or `mutateJsonState` (TypeScript) for all job state writes — never direct read-modify-write of JSON. Background jobs spawn with `setsid nohup ... &` and `disown` so they survive monitor restarts and must be re-adopted from state.
  * **Known Failure Modes**: "Job marked running but process no longer exists" → must mark `failed` with reason rather than silently delete. "Job remains running indefinitely after process exits" → result-file presence + PID liveness drives state transitions. Cleanup must respect both signals and not delete a job that is still legitimately `running`.
  * **Testing Patterns**: `tests/wavemill-job-tracker.test.ts` for unit tests; bash fixtures under `tests/fixtures/lifecycle/` for end-to-end. Synthetic long-running jobs assert monitor responsiveness.
* **Lib** (`.wavemill/context/shared-lib.md`)
  * **Key Constraints**: All JSON mutations must go through atomic helpers; fail-closed on lookup errors for wavemill-launched artifacts.
* **eval-system** (`.wavemill/context/eval-system.md`)
  * **Key Constraints**: `.wavemill/evals/evals.jsonl` is append-only training data and MUST NOT be touched by this cleanup. Only the *job-tracking* state (separate from eval rows) is in scope.

### Dependencies

* `state_mutate` (shell) / `mutateJsonState` (`shared/lib/state-mutex.ts`) — required for atomic state writes.
* `WAVEMILL_SESSION` env var — already propagated by `wavemill-startup-runner.sh` and `wavemill-mill.sh`; the cleanup logic uses this as the cleanup boundary.
* `jq` — for shell-side filtering if a shell helper is introduced.
* `tsx` — for invoking TypeScript helpers from shell phase scripts.
* Existing job-tracker contract from HOK-1564: `launch`, `poll`, `settle`, exit sentinel pattern, `evalCompleted`/`challengeCompared` flags.

### Architecture Notes

* Job state is keyed by job id and currently has fields like `id`, `pid`, `status`, `logPath`, `resultPath`, plus completion flags (`evalCompleted`, `challengeCompared`). We add an additive optional `sessionId: string` recorded at launch time.
* Cleanup is a **purge predicate** applied via `state_mutate`/`mutateJsonState`: keep jobs where `(status === 'running' && sessionId === currentSession)` OR `(sessionId === currentSession && !sideEffectsFullyApplied)`; drop the rest. This preserves the safety invariants from the manager spec.
* Two cleanup hook points:
  1. **Startup**: in `setup_control_dashboard()` / equivalent before first dashboard render in `wavemill-startup-runner.sh`. Drops everything not belonging to the current session.
  2. **Shutdown**: in the monitor's clean-exit path in `wavemill-mill.sh` (the same path that already runs end-of-session housekeeping). Drops completed/failed jobs whose side effects (`evalCompleted`/`challengeCompared`) are already applied.
* "Belongs to current session" determination: `record.sessionId === process.env.WAVEMILL_SESSION`. Legacy records without `sessionId` are treated as foreign at startup (eligible for purge) — this is safe because their PIDs cannot belong to a freshly-started session.
* Per-run resource attribution (manifest registry) is unchanged; this is purely about the live job-list.

---

## 3\. Implementation Approach

 1. **Locate the canonical job-state file path and reader/writer functions in** `shared/lib/job-tracker.ts`. Read existing `launchJob`/`pollJob`/`settleJob` to understand the record shape and the `mutateJsonState` usage pattern. Confirm whether status filtering already excludes anything (e.g., reaped jobs).
 2. **Add** `sessionId` to the persisted record at launch time. In `job-tracker.ts`, when a new job record is created, set `sessionId: process.env.WAVEMILL_SESSION ?? null`. Keep the field optional in the type so legacy records still parse.
 3. **Implement** `cleanupJobsAtSessionStart(sessionId: string)` in `job-tracker.ts`. Uses `mutateJsonState` to atomically rewrite the job-state file, retaining only records where `record.sessionId === sessionId`. Logs a single info-level message with the count of purged jobs (e.g., `[jobs] startup cleanup: purged N stale jobs from prior sessions`). Returns the number purged for observability.
 4. **Implement** `cleanupCompletedJobsAtSessionEnd(sessionId: string)` in `job-tracker.ts`. Uses `mutateJsonState` to retain only records where `(record.sessionId === sessionId)` AND (`status === 'running'` OR side effects not yet applied). The "side effects applied" predicate must check `evalCompleted` for eval jobs and `challengeCompared` for comparison jobs (extensible: future job kinds add their own flag check). Drops everything else. Returns the count purged.
 5. **Wire startup cleanup into** `shared/lib/wavemill-startup-runner.sh`. Call the cleanup TS helper (via `tsx` or by exposing a small shell wrapper) immediately before the dashboard pane is spawned, so the first render reflects the cleaned state. Place the call after `WAVEMILL_SESSION` is exported but before tmux pane spawn.
 6. **Wire shutdown cleanup into** `shared/lib/wavemill-mill.sh`. Identify the monitor's clean-exit path (already-existing trap or end-of-session block). Add an invocation of the shutdown cleanup helper there. If a clean-exit path doesn't exist, add a `trap` handler keyed to `EXIT` that calls the cleanup; the trap must be best-effort and never block exit.
 7. **Update** `shared/lib/wavemill-status.sh` rendering filter. When loading jobs for the Background jobs section, filter out records whose `sessionId` does not match the current `WAVEMILL_SESSION`. This is a defensive filter — even if cleanup hasn't run yet (race), the dashboard never shows foreign jobs. Records with missing `sessionId` are also filtered out at render time.
 8. **Add unit tests in** `shared/lib/job-tracker.test.ts`. Cover: startup cleanup drops foreign-session and legacy records; startup cleanup preserves current-session running jobs; shutdown cleanup preserves current-session running jobs; shutdown cleanup preserves jobs whose side effects haven't been applied yet; shutdown cleanup drops jobs whose side effects ARE applied. Use temp dir + `mutateJsonState` with `WAVEMILL_SESSION` overrides.
 9. **Add a lifecycle/shell test (optional but recommended) under** `tests/`. Drive `wavemill mill --dry-run` (or an equivalent fixture) with a synthetic prior-session job in state, assert it is gone after startup cleanup. Pattern after existing fixtures like `tests/wavemill-queued-tasks-state.test.sh`.
10. **Update** `docs/mill-mode.md`. Document the new behavior: jobs section is session-scoped; legacy jobs from prior sessions are cleaned at startup; completed jobs whose effects are applied are cleaned at shutdown.

---

## 4\. Success Criteria

### Functional Requirements

- [ ] **\[REQ-F1\]** When `wavemill mill` starts a new session, any records in the job-state file whose `sessionId` does not equal the current `WAVEMILL_SESSION` (including records with no `sessionId`) are removed before the dashboard renders for the first time.
- [ ] **\[REQ-F2\]** When `wavemill mill` exits cleanly, records belonging to the current session whose status is `completed` or `failed` AND whose side-effect flags (`evalCompleted` for eval jobs, `challengeCompared` for comparison jobs) are already `true` are removed from the job-state file.
- [ ] **\[REQ-F3\]** Cleanup MUST preserve any record where `status === 'running'` even if `sessionId` matches the current session (a long-running job mid-flight is not eligible for cleanup until it terminates).
- [ ] **\[REQ-F4\]** Cleanup MUST preserve any record whose required side-effect flag is `false` (e.g., a `completed` eval job whose `evalCompleted` flag has not yet been flipped by the reaper) — these still need reaping.
- [ ] **\[REQ-F5\]** New job records created via `launchJob` carry an additive `sessionId` field set to `process.env.WAVEMILL_SESSION`. Records persisted before this change continue to parse without error.
- [ ] **\[REQ-F6\]** The Background jobs dashboard section, when rendered, shows only jobs whose `sessionId` matches the current session; foreign-session and legacy records are filtered out at render time even if cleanup has not yet run.
- [ ] **\[REQ-F7\]** All cleanup mutations to the job-state file go through `mutateJsonState` (TypeScript) or `state_mutate` (shell) — verified by inspection in code review and by unit-test concurrency invariants.

### Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] Startup cleanup adds < 100ms to session startup time on a job-state file with up to 1,000 records.
- [ ] Shutdown cleanup is best-effort and never blocks process exit by more than 500ms; failures are logged and swallowed.
- [ ] No new dependencies introduced.

### Code Quality

- [ ] Follows existing codebase patterns (mutex helpers, state-additive evolution, manager subsystem rules).
- [ ] TypeScript types correct (no `any`); `sessionId` declared as optional `string | null` on the record type for legacy compatibility.
- [ ] No lint errors.

---

## 5\. Implementation Constraints

* **State mutation:** All writes to `.wavemill/state/monitored-jobs.json` MUST use `mutateJsonState` (TS) or `state_mutate` (shell). Direct `readFileSync` + `writeFileSync` is forbidden (manager spec).
* **Schema evolution:** `sessionId` MUST be optional on the record type and JSON shape. Records missing the field MUST parse without throwing. This is the additive evolution pattern used across the codebase (queue plan metadata, eval schema, etc.).
* **Safety invariants:** Cleanup MUST NOT delete a record where `status === 'running'`, regardless of session. Cleanup MUST NOT delete a record where the relevant side-effect flag is `false`.
* **Background jobs vs. eval JSONL:** `.wavemill/evals/evals.jsonl` is OUT OF SCOPE — that is append-only training data. Only `.wavemill/state/monitored-jobs.json` (or equivalent) is touched.
* **Session boundary:** `WAVEMILL_SESSION` is the cleanup key. Do not invent a new session id; use the value already set by the startup runner.
* **Logging:** Cleanup emits at most one info-level line per phase (startup / shutdown) summarizing the count purged. No per-record logging. Use the task-id-prefixed logger only when running inside a task scope; cleanup is session-scoped, so plain INFO is fine.
* **Shutdown safety:** Shutdown cleanup runs in a `trap`/clean-exit path and MUST NOT throw out of the trap; wrap in try/catch and log on failure.
* **Backwards compatibility:** A monitor restart mid-session must NOT lose running jobs — `setsid nohup ... & disown` survives, and re-adoption depends on the record persisting. Cleanup at startup looks at sessionId match, so an in-place restart (same `WAVEMILL_SESSION`) preserves everything. A new session deliberately purges, which is the desired behavior.
* **Testing:** Use existing test patterns (`tests/wavemill-job-tracker.test.ts` style). Use temp directories and `WAVEMILL_SESSION` env overrides to isolate state.

---

## 6\. Validation Steps

### Functional Requirement Validation

**\[REQ-F1\] Startup cleanup drops foreign-session and legacy records**

Validation scenario:

1. Setup: Create a temp wavemill state dir with `monitored-jobs.json` containing three records: A (sessionId=`old-session-1`, status=`completed`), B (no sessionId field, status=`failed`), C (sessionId=`current-session`, status=`running`).
2. Action: Set `WAVEMILL_SESSION=current-session` and call `cleanupJobsAtSessionStart('current-session')`.
3. Expected result: `monitored-jobs.json` now contains only record C. Function returns `2` (count purged).
4. Edge cases:
   * State file does not exist → cleanup is a no-op, returns `0`, no error thrown.
   * State file is empty array `[]` → cleanup is a no-op, returns `0`.
   * State file contains malformed JSON → cleanup logs error, returns `0`, does not throw out of caller.

**\[REQ-F2\] Shutdown cleanup drops completed-and-reaped jobs from current session**

Validation scenario:

1. Setup: State file contains four records, all `sessionId=current-session`: D (`status=running`), E (`status=completed`, `evalCompleted=true`), F (`status=completed`, `evalCompleted=false`), G (`status=failed`, `challengeCompared=true`, kind=comparison).
2. Action: Call `cleanupCompletedJobsAtSessionEnd('current-session')`.
3. Expected result: State file retains D and F; E and G are removed. Function returns `2`.
4. Edge cases:
   * All jobs running → no-op, returns `0`.
   * All jobs completed-and-reaped → all removed, returns total count.
   * Mixed-session contents → only current-session reaped jobs are removed; other-session records are left untouched (those are startup cleanup's responsibility).

**\[REQ-F3\] Running jobs are preserved**

Validation scenario:

1. Setup: State file contains record H (sessionId=`current-session`, status=`running`, pid=alive PID, evalCompleted=false).
2. Action: Run both startup and shutdown cleanup back-to-back.
3. Expected result: H is still present in the state file after both calls.
4. Edge cases:
   * Stale `running` record where pid no longer exists → still preserved by cleanup (poll/settle is responsible for transitioning status, not cleanup).

**\[REQ-F4\] Unreaped completed jobs are preserved**

Validation scenario:

1. Setup: Record I (sessionId=current, status=`completed`, kind=`eval`, `evalCompleted=false`).
2. Action: Call `cleanupCompletedJobsAtSessionEnd('current-session')`.
3. Expected result: I remains in state file.
4. Edge cases:
   * Record with status=`failed` but `evalCompleted=false` → preserved (operator may want to inspect).

**\[REQ-F5\] New jobs carry sessionId; legacy records still parse**

Validation scenario:

1. Setup: Set `WAVEMILL_SESSION=test-session-42`. Manually seed a legacy record without `sessionId`.
2. Action: Call `launchJob({...})` to add a new record. Then read state.
3. Expected result: New record has `sessionId: 'test-session-42'`. Legacy record still loads (no JSON parse error, no schema validation error).
4. Edge cases:
   * `WAVEMILL_SESSION` unset → new record `sessionId` is `null` or omitted; cleanup treats it as foreign (eligible for purge next startup).

**\[REQ-F6\] Status renderer filters foreign records**

Validation scenario:

1. Setup: State file contains current-session record + foreign-session record. Cleanup is intentionally NOT yet run.
2. Action: Render the Background jobs dashboard section.
3. Expected result: Only the current-session record appears. Foreign record is not displayed.
4. Edge cases:
   * All records foreign → section renders as empty (or "no active jobs"), not as a list of stale entries.

**\[REQ-F7\] All mutations use atomic helpers**

Validation scenario:

1. Setup: Code review of `cleanupJobsAtSessionStart` and `cleanupCompletedJobsAtSessionEnd`.
2. Action: Grep for `writeFileSync` / `fs.writeFile` calls inside these functions.
3. Expected result: Zero direct writes; all paths flow through `mutateJsonState`.
4. Edge cases:
   * Concurrent monitor restart triggering cleanup while a launch is in flight → `mutateJsonState`'s file lock serializes; no torn writes.

---

### Input/Output Verification

**Valid Inputs:**

* Job state with mixed sessions and statuses → Cleanup retains only current-session running + unreaped records.
* Empty state file `[]` → Returns 0, file unchanged.
* Missing state file → Returns 0, no file created.

**Invalid Inputs:**

* Malformed JSON in state file → Logs error, returns 0, does not crash caller. State file is left untouched (or quarantined per existing job-tracker conventions).
* `sessionId` argument is empty string → Treat as a no-match: every record's `sessionId !== ''` so all records get purged at startup. Should be defensive — if `WAVEMILL_SESSION` is unset, cleanup logs a warning and skips (rather than nuking everything).

# Investigate codebase for cleanup opportunities - Quick Reference

**Issue ID**: HOK-1624

## Objective

Investigate the wavemill repository for unused code and stale top-level directories, focusing on the `agents/` directory, four named skills under `skills/`, the `.wavemill-config.json.backup` file, and `fixtures/plan-queue`. Remove confirmed-unused artifacts in a single PR while documenting any directories that look stale but cannot be confirmed unused.

## Key Files

* `agents/` (directory under investigation)
* `skills/document-orchestrator/`, `skills/frontend-design/`, `skills/frontend-testing/`, `skills/git-workflow-manager/`, `skills/issue-writer/`, `skills/linear-task-selector/` (skills under investigation)
* `.wavemill-config.json.backup` (file to remove)
* `fixtures/plan-queue/` (directory under investigation)
* `features/` (top-level state directory under investigation; may contain stale per-feature subfolders)

## Critical Constraints

1. **Verify before deleting** — Every removal must be backed by a documented, repo-wide search (`rg`/`grep`) showing zero references from runtime code, shell scripts, prompts, docs, tests, or CI workflows. Record the searches performed in the PR description.
2. **No scope creep into refactors** — This task is removal-only. Do not rename, move, or refactor remaining code. If a directory has any active references, leave it alone and document why in the investigation report.
3. **Preserve auto-generated and gitignored state** — Do not touch `.wavemill/registry/`, `.wavemill/manifests/`, `.wavemill/evals/`, `/tmp/wavemill-*`, or anything excluded by `.gitignore`. These are runtime state, not source.

## Success Criteria (High-Level)

- [ ] Each item under investigation (`agents/`, the named skills, `.wavemill-config.json.backup`, `fixtures/plan-queue`, plus other top-level directories surveyed) has a documented usage decision: removed-with-evidence, kept-with-justification, or deferred-with-reason.
- [ ] All confirmed-unused files and directories are deleted in a single PR; commit message references HOK-1624.
- [ ] Remaining tests, lint, typecheck, and shell tests pass with no regressions caused by the removals.
- [ ] PR description includes an investigation report listing every top-level directory inspected and the search evidence supporting each removal or retention decision.
- [ ] Tests and lint pass; PR created and linked to HOK-1624.

## 1\. Objective

### What

Investigate the wavemill repository for unused or stale top-level artifacts, then remove the ones that can be conclusively shown to be unused. The primary investigation targets are: the `agents/` directory, the skills called out as suspect in the issue (under `skills/`), `.wavemill-config.json.backup`, and `fixtures/plan-queue`. Any other top-level directory that looks stale (e.g. completed feature folders) must also be surveyed, with a documented decision per directory.

### Why

The repo has accumulated artifacts from earlier experiments and finished work (per-feature scratch dirs, leftover backup configs, fixtures from already-shipped epics). Carrying these forward inflates the directory tree shown to every issue-expansion run, raises the surface area agents must reason about, and creates ambiguity about which subsystems are still load-bearing. Pruning unused top-level directories directly improves agent context quality and lowers maintenance noise.

### Scope In

* Audit the four explicit targets called out in the issue:
  * `agents/` directory
  * The named skills under `skills/` (note: directory listing currently shows six skills — `document-orchestrator`, `frontend-design`, `frontend-testing`, `git-workflow-manager`, `issue-writer`, `linear-task-selector`. Investigate all of them; the issue's "four skills" wording is approximate.)
  * `.wavemill-config.json.backup`
  * `fixtures/plan-queue`
* Survey every other top-level directory in the repo for staleness signals (no recent git activity, no inbound references, content describes already-shipped work).
* For every item: run repo-wide reference searches and record the evidence.
* Remove confirmed-unused items (files and directories) in a single cleanup PR.
* Update or remove any docs that referenced the removed paths so docs stay truthful.

### Scope Out

* Refactoring or renaming code that is kept (no scope creep).
* Touching `.wavemill/registry/`, `.wavemill/manifests/`, `.wavemill/evals/`, or other runtime state directories.
* Modifying `.gitignore` semantics, branch policies, or CI workflows beyond removing references to deleted paths.
* Investigating files inside `node_modules/`, `dist/`, or any build output (these are not committed top-level artifacts).
* Deleting anything with even a single live inbound reference; ambiguous cases are reported, not deleted.
* Compacting or pruning `.wavemill/project-context.md` (separate concern, owned by `tools/compact-project-context.ts`).

## 2\. Technical Context

### Repository

Single repo: `wavemill` (this repo). All work happens in the worktree `worktrees/investigate-codebase-for-cleanup-opportunities` on branch `task/investigate-codebase-for-cleanup-opportunities`.

### Key Files

Investigation targets and likely-modified paths:

* `agents/` — directory under investigation; remove if confirmed unused.

  * `features/add-integration-test-for-dashboard-layout/`
  * `features/add-lint-operation-for-specs/`
  * `features/bug-control-pane-crashed/`

### Relevant Subsystem Specs

The specs surfaced in context (`router.md`, `eval-system.md`, `quota-tracking.md`) are not directly relevant to a cleanup task. ### Dependencies

### Architecture Notes

* **Single Source of Truth principle (CLAUDE.md)**: The repo treats `shared/lib/` as canonical for business logic and `tools/` as thin wrappers. A directory like `agents/` or `skills/` that has no inbound reference from `shared/lib/`, `tools/`, `commands/`, `codex/src/`, `tests/`, or `docs/` is a strong removal candidate.
* **Reference-search heuristic**: A path is "in use" if any of these reference it:
  * TypeScript/JavaScript imports (`from '...'`, `require('...')`, `import('...')`)
  * Shell script `source` or path arguments
  * Markdown links from `docs/`, `commands/`, `codex/prompts/`, `tools/prompts/`

* **Skills directory pattern**: Inspect `skills/*/SKILL.md` (or whatever convention the repo uses) for declared entry points and search for those identifiers across the codebase. If a skill is invoked by name (e.g. as a string in agent configuration) the search must include the skill folder name as a literal string.
* **Features directory pattern**: `features/<kebab-case-name>/` folders are typically per-feature scratch directories owned by Claude Code workflow. They contain plans, notes, and intermediate artifacts. A folder whose corresponding Linear issue is `Done` and whose contents have not been touched in >30 days is a strong removal candidate, but only if nothing else in the repo references it.
* **Investigation report format**: Treat the investigation as a deliverable in its own right. The PR body must include a table with one row per top-level directory: `directory | status (kept/removed/deferred) | evidence`.

## 5\. Implementation Constraints

* **Verification is non-negotiable.** Never delete a path without a documented `rg`/`grep` search showing zero inbound references. The PR must be able to answer "how do you know nothing depends on this?" for every removed path.
* **Removal-only diff.** Do not refactor, rename, or reformat code in this PR. The only allowed additions are doc edits that strip references to removed paths. If you discover refactoring opportunities, file a follow-up — do not bundle them.
* **Preserve runtime state.** Do not touch `.wavemill/registry/`, `.wavemill/manifests/`, `.wavemill/evals/`, `/tmp/wavemill-*`, or anything in `.gitignore`. These are not source code.
* **Preserve this task's scratch folder.** `features/investigate-codebase-for-cleanup-opportunities/` must remain.
* **Handle ambiguity by deferring.** If a directory looks stale but has even one suspicious-but-unclear reference, mark it `deferred` in the report and leave it. False-positive deletions are worse than false-negative retentions in a cleanup task.
* **Use** `git rm -r`, not `rm -rf`. Stage deletions through git so the PR diff is clean and reversible.
* **No supply-chain or destructive shortcuts.** Do not use `git filter-branch`, `git rebase -i` to reorder published commits, or any history-rewriting operation. Keep the PR a simple feature-branch removal.
* **Tests must continue to pass.** Run the full validation suite locally before opening the PR. Treat any new test failure as a signal to restore the removed path.
* **Commit message references the issue.** Use `HOK-1624` in the commit message and PR title.

**\[REQ-F1\] Inventory and decision table exist in PR**

Validation scenario:

1. Setup: PR is open against `main` with the cleanup branch.
2. Action: Open the PR description and locate the "Investigation Report" section.
3. Expected result: A markdown table is present with columns `directory_or_file | status | evidence`. 2. Action: Run `git ls-files | grep -F '.wavemill-config.json.backup'`.
3. Expected result: Empty output (file no longer tracked).
4. Edge cases:

Validation scenario:

1. Setup: PR branch checked out.
2. Action: Run `git ls-files agents/ 2>/dev/null | wc -l` and inspect the investigation report row for `agents/`.

   * `agents/` removed but a doc still references it → REQ-F6 fails; update the doc.

**\[REQ-F4\] Each skill has a documented decision**

Validation scenario:

2. Action: For each skill in `{document-orchestrator, frontend-design, frontend-testing, git-workflow-manager, issue-writer, linear-task-selector}`, run `git ls-files skills/<skill>/ | wc -l` and find its row in the investigation report.

# HOK-1582: Reduce and move Jobs section

# Reduce and move Jobs section - Quick Reference

**Issue ID**: HOK-1582

## Objective

Move the JOBS, PENDING DEPENDENCY, and QUEUED COMMANDS sections off the main dashboard pane and into a redesigned 3-pane "backstage" tmux window. The dashboard becomes focused (INBOX + ACTIVE only), while informational background state moves to dedicated panes alongside the tend loop. Also rename windows: `control` → `mill`, `integration` → `backstage`.

## Key Files

* `shared/lib/wavemill-status.sh` (lines 713-771: render functions to extract; dashboard rendering)
* `shared/lib/wavemill-startup-runner.sh` (lines 369-389: `spawn_integration_window`; window naming)
* `shared/lib/wavemill-common.sh` (window-name constants/references, if present)
* `shared/lib/wavemill-mill.sh` (mill loop references to window names)
* `tests/task-selection-renderer.test.sh` (existing dashboard render coverage; add/adjust assertions)

## Critical Constraints

1. **Preserve existing render logic** — extract `render_jobs_section`, `render_queued_section`, `render_monitor_command_queue_section` without changing their output semantics; only trim column widths to fit narrower (\~50% width) panes.
2. **Maintain shellcheck cleanliness** — all extracted scripts must pass `tests/check-shell.sh` and follow the existing `wavemill-*.sh` style (source `wavemill-common.sh`, use `state_mutate` for any JSON writes).
3. **Window-name rename must be repo-wide** — every reference to `control` and `integration` window names (in shell, docs, tests) must update consistently to `mill` and `backstage` respectively, with no orphaned literals.

## Success Criteria (High-Level)

- [ ] Dashboard pane renders only INBOX + ACTIVE sections (no JOBS, PENDING, or QUEUED)
- [ ] Backstage window has 3 panes: tend loop (left, \~60%), Jobs (top-right), Pending+Queued (bottom-right)
- [ ] Each backstage pane refreshes on a loop comparable to the dashboard's cadence
- [ ] Window names are `mill` and `backstage` everywhere (shell, docs, tests)
- [ ] JOBS table format trimmed to fit \~40-column width without breaking columns
- [ ] Tests and lint pass; `tests/check-shell.sh` clean
- [ ] PR created and linked to HOK-1582

## 1\. Objective

### What

Reduce the wavemill dashboard to two attention-demanding sections (INBOX, ACTIVE) and relocate the three informational background sections (JOBS, PENDING DEPENDENCY, QUEUED COMMANDS) into a redesigned 3-pane tmux window currently called `integration` (renamed to `backstage`). The `control` window is renamed to `mill`.

### Why

The current dashboard mixes high-attention items (tasks needing user action) with informational background state, creating visual noise and pushing important sections below the fold. The integration window is underutilized (only one pane running tend loop), making it the natural home for background information that benefits from continuous visibility but doesn't require immediate user attention. Renaming `control` → `mill` and `integration` → `backstage` aligns the window names with their actual purpose in the wavemill mental model.

### Scope In

* Extract `render_jobs_section`, `render_queued_section`, `render_monitor_command_queue_section` from `shared/lib/wavemill-status.sh` (lines 713–771) into independently-runnable render scripts (or extracted shell functions invokable from a thin entry script).
* Remove the JOBS, PENDING DEPENDENCY, and QUEUED COMMANDS sections from the dashboard render path, leaving INBOX + ACTIVE.
* Modify `spawn_integration_window` in `shared/lib/wavemill-startup-runner.sh` (lines 369–389) to split the window into 3 panes per the layout in the issue.
* Add per-pane refresh loops for the two new background panes (jobs pane and pending+queued pane) using a refresh cadence comparable to the dashboard.
* Rename the `control` window to `mill` and the `integration` window to `backstage` everywhere they are referenced.
* Trim the JOBS table reporting line so it fits at \~50% width (≈40 columns).
* Update tests and docs to reflect the new layout and naming.

### Scope Out

* Changing the visual styling (colors, glyphs) of the rendered sections beyond the JOBS column-width trim required to fit.
* Adding new sources of data (no new state files, no new commands).
* Reworking the tend loop itself.
* Adding configurability for pane sizes (the 60/50/50 split is hardcoded).
* Persisting window-rename for users with existing tmux sessions (sessions are recreated each `wavemill mill` start).

---

## 2\. Technical Context

### Repository

`wavemill` — current working repo. All changes are within this repo; no cross-repo coordination needed.

### Key Files

* `shared/lib/wavemill-status.sh` (lines 713–771) — Existing render functions for jobs, queued, monitor-command-queue sections; also contains the dashboard-loop main render path that must drop these sections.
* `shared/lib/wavemill-startup-runner.sh` (lines 369–389) — `spawn_integration_window` and `setup_control_dashboard` define current window/pane layout; window naming originates here.
* `shared/lib/wavemill-common.sh` — Common helpers (`state_mutate`, env vars, possibly window-name constants); referenced by hooks and dashboard for `WAVEMILL_DASHBOARD_PID` propagation.
* `shared/lib/wavemill-mill.sh` — Mill loop; may reference window names when targeting tmux operations.
* `shared/lib/agent-adapters.sh` — `agent_resolve_dashboard_pid()` uses tmux session env; ensure no hard-coded `control`/`integration` window references remain.
* `shared/hooks/wavemill-hook-protocol.sh` and `shared/hooks/claude-status-hook.sh` — Use `WAVEMILL_DASHBOARD_PID` for signal-driven refresh; verify the rename doesn't break PID propagation.
* `tests/check-shell.sh` — Shellcheck gate; new scripts must pass.
* `tests/task-selection-renderer.test.sh` — Existing dashboard render coverage; will need adjustments since sections are removed.
* `tests/fixtures/startup/` — Likely contains startup-related fixtures referencing window names.
* `docs/mill-mode.md` — Public-facing documentation likely references `control`/`integration` windows by name.
* `docs/lifecycle-tests.md` — May reference window names in setup instructions.

### Relevant Subsystem Specs

⚠️ **Knowledge Gap**: No subsystem specs found specifically for the dashboard/tmux-window layout subsystem (`wavemill-status.sh`, `wavemill-startup-runner.sh`). The provided router and quota-tracking specs are not relevant to this UI/layout task. After implementation, consider running `wavemill context init --force` to create subsystem documentation for the dashboard-rendering and startup-runner subsystems and enable persistent downstream acceleration for future tasks.

### Dependencies

* `tmux` — Window/pane management (already required by wavemill).
* `jq` — JSON parsing for state files (already required).
* No new external packages.

### Architecture Notes

* **Single-source-of-truth render functions**: Extracted render functions should remain in `shared/lib/` (e.g., either kept in `wavemill-status.sh` and invoked via flag, or moved to a new sourced helper file) so the dashboard, jobs pane, and queued pane all call the same shell functions. **Do NOT duplicate rendering logic**.
* **Pane entrypoints**: The cleanest pattern is to add small entrypoint scripts (or new flags on `wavemill-status.sh`, e.g., `wavemill-status.sh --pane=jobs`, `wavemill-status.sh --pane=queued-pending`) that loop with `sleep` and call the extracted functions. Reuse the existing `WAVEMILL_DASHBOARD_REFRESH_SECONDS` env override pattern for cadence, but introduce per-pane env (`WAVEMILL_BACKSTAGE_REFRESH_SECONDS`) only if needed; otherwise reuse the dashboard refresh.
* **Signal-driven refresh**: The existing `USR1` signal pattern targets `$WAVEMILL_DASHBOARD_PID`. Decide whether the new backstage panes also wake on `USR1` — likely yes for the jobs pane (writes to job state files would benefit from immediate refresh). Track each pane's PID similarly via a tmux session env var (e.g., `WAVEMILL_BACKSTAGE_JOBS_PID`, `WAVEMILL_BACKSTAGE_QUEUED_PID`) and have writers call `wavemill_hook_notify` for each registered listener. **For this task, default behavior**: poll-based refresh is sufficient — only add signal hookup if it's trivial. Document the trade-off either way.
* **Window-name constants**: Introduce `WAVEMILL_WINDOW_MILL="mill"` and `WAVEMILL_WINDOW_BACKSTAGE="backstage"` in `wavemill-common.sh` (if not already present as constants) so future renames are one-place changes. Replace literal `control` / `integration` strings throughout.
* **JOBS table width**: Current format `%-10s %-18s %6s` plus status and log basename ≈ 50+ chars. At 50% of an 80-col terminal (\~40 chars usable), this overflows. Trim to fit by either (a) shortening column widths (e.g., `%-8s %-12s %5s`), (b) dropping the log-basename column when narrow, or (c) truncating long values with `…`. Pick the option that preserves the most-essential identifiers (id, status, elapsed).

## 3\. Implementation Approach

 1. **Audit current render path** — Read `shared/lib/wavemill-status.sh` lines 700–800 to confirm the exact function names, signatures, and the dashboard loop that calls them. Note any shared state/env they read.
 2. **Audit window-name references** — `grep -rn 'control\|integration' shared/ tests/ docs/` to enumerate all literal references that must change. Distinguish window-name uses from CI/integration uses (e.g., `auto/integration` branch names must NOT be renamed).
 3. **Introduce window-name constants** in `shared/lib/wavemill-common.sh` (or top of `wavemill-startup-runner.sh` if `wavemill-common.sh` isn't appropriate): `WAVEMILL_WINDOW_MILL="mill"` and `WAVEMILL_WINDOW_BACKSTAGE="backstage"`. Replace literals across the codebase.
 4. **Refactor extracted render functions** — Confirm `render_jobs_section`, `render_queued_section`, `render_monitor_command_queue_section` are pure render functions (no side effects beyond stdout). Add a top-level dispatcher in `wavemill-status.sh` so it can run in different modes:
    * Default / no flag: dashboard mode (INBOX + ACTIVE only — JOBS/PENDING/QUEUED removed).
    * `--pane=jobs`: loop calling `render_jobs_section`.
    * `--pane=queued-pending`: loop calling `render_queued_section` and `render_monitor_command_queue_section`.
 5. **Trim JOBS table format** — Update the format string at `wavemill-status.sh:741` to fit \~40 columns. Suggested: `%-8s %-12s %5s` plus a truncated/optional log basename. Verify with sample data that no column overflows visibly at 40-col width.
 6. **Remove dropped sections from dashboard** — In the dashboard render loop, delete (or guard with a `mode != dashboard` check) the calls to the three relocated render functions. Ensure section headers, separators, and ordering for INBOX + ACTIVE remain intact.
 7. **Update** `spawn_integration_window` — In `wavemill-startup-runner.sh:369–389`:
    * Rename window to `backstage` (use the new constant).
    * After spawning pane 0 with the tend loop, `tmux split-window -h -p 40` (or `-l 40%`) to create pane 1 to the right.
    * Then `tmux split-window -v -t pane1 -p 50` to split pane 1 vertically into top (jobs) and bottom (pending+queued).
    * `respawn-pane` each new pane with the appropriate `wavemill-status.sh --pane=...` invocation, ensuring the env vars (`WAVEMILL_SESSION`, `WAVEMILL_DASHBOARD_PID`, etc.) propagate.
    * Verify pane indices are predictable; if tmux's split logic produces different indices, capture them via `tmux split-window -P -F '#{pane_id}'`.
 8. **Rename control window** — In `setup_control_dashboard` (or wherever the window is named), use the `WAVEMILL_WINDOW_MILL` constant. Update any `tmux select-window -t :control` or similar references.
 9. **Update mill loop / hooks** — Search for any `tmux` commands targeting `:control` or `:integration` by name (vs index) in `shared/lib/wavemill-mill.sh`, `shared/hooks/`, and update them to use the new constants/names.
10. **Update tests** — Adjust `tests/task-selection-renderer.test.sh` so dashboard render assertions no longer expect JOBS/PENDING/QUEUED. Add new test(s) verifying the pane modes render the expected sections. Update `tests/fixtures/startup/` if it asserts window names.
11. **Update docs** — `docs/mill-mode.md` and any other doc mentioning `control`/`integration` windows: rename to `mill`/`backstage` and describe the new 3-pane backstage layout.
12. **Run validation gates** — `tests/check-shell.sh` (shellcheck), targeted shell tests, full test suite. Manually start `wavemill mill` in a scratch repo and visually confirm both windows render correctly.

## 4\. Success Criteria

### Functional Requirements

- [ ] **\[REQ-F1\]** Dashboard pane (in the `mill` window) renders ONLY the INBOX and ACTIVE sections. JOBS, PENDING DEPENDENCY, and QUEUED COMMANDS section headers are absent from dashboard output.
- [ ] **\[REQ-F2\]** The window currently named `integration` is renamed to `backstage`; the window currently named `control` is renamed to `mill`. `tmux list-windows -t <session>` shows exactly these names (no `control` or `integration` windows remain).
- [ ] **\[REQ-F3\]** The `backstage` window contains exactly 3 panes laid out as: pane 0 left (\~60% width) running the tend loop; pane 1 top-right (\~50% of right column) running the Jobs render; pane 2 bottom-right (\~50% of right column) running combined Pending Dependency + Queued Commands render.
- [ ] **\[REQ-F4\]** Each new backstage pane (jobs, pending+queued) refreshes its content on a loop without manual input. The refresh cadence matches the dashboard (default 2s, overridable via existing or new env var).
- [ ] **\[REQ-F5\]** The JOBS table fits within \~40 columns of pane width without column wrapping or visible truncation artifacts (other than intentional `…` truncation indicators).
- [ ] **\[REQ-F6\]** The render functions `render_jobs_section`, `render_queued_section`, `render_monitor_command_queue_section` are NOT duplicated — they exist in exactly one location and are reused by the backstage pane entrypoints.
- [ ] **\[REQ-F7\]** No literal references to the old window names `control` or `integration` (as window targets) remain in shell scripts, tests, or docs. References to `auto/integration` (branch name) and `tools/init-project-context.ts` (unrelated `integration` strings) are NOT modified.

### Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] All shell scripts pass `tests/check-shell.sh` (shellcheck) with no new warnings.
- [ ] No measurable startup-time regression (<200ms additional time for `wavemill mill` cold start).
- [ ] No additional persistent file handles or background processes beyond the 2 new pane refresh loops.

### Code Quality

- [ ] Follows existing `shared/lib/wavemill-*.sh` patterns (sourcing `wavemill-common.sh`, using `state_mutate` for any JSON writes, env var naming).
- [ ] No `any`/loose-typed shell — all variables quoted, error handling consistent with existing scripts.
- [ ] No dead code: dashboard render path should not contain commented-out section calls; remove them entirely.

## 5\. Implementation Constraints

* **Code style**: Match `shared/lib/wavemill-*.sh` conventions — `set -euo pipefail` (where used), all variables quoted, no `eval`, source `wavemill-common.sh` for shared helpers.
* **Single source of truth for render logic**: Extracted render functions must NOT be duplicated. Either (a) keep them in `wavemill-status.sh` and invoke via mode flag, or (b) move them to a sourced helper file (e.g., `shared/lib/wavemill-render-sections.sh`) and source from both contexts. Pick one; don't copy-paste.
* **State writes**: Any JSON state read-modify-write MUST use `state_mutate` from `wavemill-common.sh`. Append-only logs and `/tmp/wavemill-*.hook` files keep their existing patterns.
* **Window-name discipline**: Replace ALL literal references to `control`/`integration` window names. Do NOT rename `auto/integration` branch references, CI/CD "integration" terminology, or `tools/init-project-context.ts` calls — only tmux window-name uses.
* **Backwards compatibility**: Tmux sessions are ephemeral per `wavemill mill` start, so no migration needed for live sessions. But any external scripts/aliases that target windows by name (if documented) should be flagged in the PR description.
* **Testing**: New rendering modes must be testable headlessly. Prefer functions that produce deterministic stdout given fixture state files. Avoid coupling tests to actual tmux invocation.
* **Security**: No new external commands invoked with unsanitized input. All `tmux` commands use quoted arguments.
* **Performance**: New refresh loops MUST use `sleep "$REFRESH" &; wait` pattern (matching dashboard) so they wake on signals if the signal mechanism is extended; otherwise plain `sleep` is acceptable for this task.
* **Docs sync**: Any user-facing docs that mention window names must be updated in the same PR.

## 6\. Validation Steps

### Functional Requirement Validation

**\[REQ-F1\] Dashboard renders only INBOX + ACTIVE**

Validation scenario:

1. Setup: In a wavemill-enabled scratch repo, populate state with a mix of inbox tasks, active tasks, jobs, pending-dep tasks, and queued commands using the existing test fixtures (or by running `wavemill mill` once).
2. Action: Run `bash shared/lib/wavemill-status.sh` (dashboard mode, default) and capture stdout to a file.
3. Expected result: Output contains "INBOX" and "ACTIVE" headers; output does NOT contain "JOBS", "PENDING DEPENDENCY", or "QUEUED COMMANDS" headers.
4. Edge cases:
   * Empty state (no tasks anywhere) → Dashboard still shows INBOX/ACTIVE headers with empty bodies, no errors.
   * State with only jobs (no inbox/active) → Dashboard shows empty INBOX/ACTIVE; jobs do NOT appear.

**\[REQ-F2\] Window rename verification**

Validation scenario:

1. Setup: Start a fresh wavemill session: `wavemill mill` in a test repo.
2. Action: Run `tmux list-windows -t <session-name> -F '#{window_name}'`.
3. Expected result: Output is exactly `mill\nbackstage` (in some order); no `control` or `integration` strings appear.
4. Edge cases:
   * Session name contains hyphens or special chars → Window names still resolve correctly.
   * Re-run `wavemill mill` against an existing session → Windows are reused with the new names (or recreated, depending on existing behavior; document which).

**\[REQ-F3\] Backstage 3-pane layout**

Validation scenario:

1. Setup: Start a fresh wavemill session.
2. Action: Run `tmux list-panes -t <session>:backstage -F '#{pane_index} #{pane_width} #{pane_height} #{pane_current_command}'`.
3. Expected result: 3 panes; pane 0 width ≈ 60% of window width; panes 1 and 2 each ≈ 40% width (right column) and ≈ 50% of window height each. Pane 0 runs tend; panes 1 and 2 run wavemill-status (or equivalent).
4. Edge cases:
   * Window resized very small (<80 cols total) → Layout still creates 3 panes; rendered content gracefully degrades (truncation acceptable).
   * tmux version variance → Use `-l <pct>%` syntax compatible with tmux ≥ 2.6 (current minimum supported by wavemill, verify in repo).

**\[REQ-F4\] Pane refresh loops**

Validation scenario:

1. Setup: Start wavemill mill in a test repo with at least 1 job and 1 queued command.
2. Action: Capture pane 1 (jobs) content via `tmux capture-pane -p -t <session>:backstage.1`. Modify the underlying jobs state file (e.g., add a row). Wait 3 seconds. Capture again.
3. Expected result: Second capture reflects the new row without manual intervention.
4. Edge cases:
   * State file deleted while pane is running → Pane shows empty/no-data state, no crash.
   * Refresh cadence env override `WAVEMILL_DASHBOARD_REFRESH_SECONDS=5` → Pane refreshes at 5s cadence (verify timing approximate).

**\[REQ-F5\] JOBS table fits \~40 columns**

Validation scenario:

1. Setup: Create a fixture jobs state file with 3 rows containing realistic-length values (e.g., id `job-12345`, status `running`, elapsed `12m34s`, log basename `wavemill-task-foo-bar.log`).
2. Action: Run jobs render in pane mode, pipe through `awk '{ if (length > 42) print NR": "length" "$0 }'` to find lines exceeding 42 chars.
3. Expected result: No lines exceed 42 chars (allowing 2-char buffer for terminal padding).
4. Edge cases:
   * Job id longer than column width → Truncated with `…` indicator, not wrapped.
   * Empty jobs state → Render produces just the header line, ≤ 42 chars.

**\[REQ-F6\] No render-function duplication**

Validation scenario:

1. Setup: Repo with the implementation complete.
2. Action: Run `grep -rn 'render_jobs_section\s*()' shared/`.
3. Expected result: Exactly one definition (one `render_jobs_section() {` line). Same for `render_queued_section` and `render_monitor_command_queue_section`.
4. Edge cases:
   * Function defined in two files (regression) → Test fails, surfacing duplication.

**\[REQ-F7\] No stale window-name literals**

Validation scenario:

1. Setup: Implementation complete.
2. Action: Run `grep -rn -E 'tmux .*(:|-t )(control|integration)\b' shared/ tests/ docs/`.
3. Expected result: No matches (no tmux commands targeting old window names).
4. Edge cases:
   * References to `auto/integration` branch → NOT matched (regex anchors `:` or `-t ` immediately before name).
   * References to "integration tests" in comments/docs → NOT matched.

# HOK-1626: Rotating usage tips at bottom of Dashboard.

# Rotating Usage Tips at Bottom of Dashboard - Quick Reference

**Issue ID**: HOK-1626

## Objective

Replace the static dashboard footer line ("Refreshes every 2s │ Ctrl+B <PANE>: switch task │ Ctrl+B N: next done") with a rotating selection from a curated list of 10 wavemill usage tips. Each refresh cycle randomly chooses a tip to surface non-obvious functionality (auto-cleanup, auto-merge, CLI commands, config options) to users. Keep the existing refresh/keyboard hints somewhere visible while rotating the rest.

## Key Files

* `shared/lib/wavemill-status.sh` — dashboard footer rendering (status/help line)
* `shared/lib/wavemill-mill.sh` — mill-mode dashboard composition
* `shared/lib/wavemill-common.sh` — shared helpers used by status rendering
* `tests/wavemill-status.test.sh` — dashboard rendering tests
* `docs/mill-mode.md` — user-facing documentation for mill dashboard

## Critical Constraints

1. **Each tip must fit on a single line** at typical terminal widths (≤ 100 chars including separators) — no wrapping in dashboard footer.
2. **Tips must be factually accurate** — every command, flag, or config key must be verifiable against the current codebase (e.g., `WAVEMILL_DASHBOARD_REFRESH_SECONDS`, `wavemill expand`, `.wavemill-config.json` keys).
3. **Rotation must not destabilize the dashboard** — selection happens per render tick and must be deterministic-per-tick (no flicker mid-render), and must not break the existing `USR1`-driven refresh path.

## Success Criteria (High-Level)

- [ ] Static footer line is replaced by a rotating tip selected from a curated list of 10 tips.
- [ ] Each tip is short, accurate, and surfaces non-obvious wavemill functionality.
- [ ] Dashboard refresh cadence and `USR1` signal-driven updates continue to work unchanged.
- [ ] Tests cover tip list integrity (count, length, no duplicates) and rotation behavior.
- [ ] Tests and shellcheck pass; PR created and linked to HOK-1626.

## Detailed Sections

Full details available on-demand in task-packet-details.md:

* [Section 1: Complete Objective & Scope](<#1-objective>)
* [Section 2: Technical Context](<#2-technical-context>)
* [Section 3: Implementation Approach](<#3-implementation-approach>)
* [Section 4: Success Criteria](<#4-success-criteria>)
* [Section 5: Implementation Constraints](<#5-implementation-constraints>)
* [Section 6: Validation Steps](<#6-validation-steps>)
* [Section 8: Definition of Done](<#8-definition-of-done>)
* [Section 9: Rollback Plan](<#9-rollback-plan>)
* [Section 10: Release Readiness](<#10-release-readiness>)
* [Section 11: Proposed Labels](<#11-proposed-labels>)

**Implementation Note**: Start with this overview. Read detailed sections on-demand as you implement.

---

## 1\. Objective

### What

Replace the static dashboard footer hint line in `shared/lib/wavemill-status.sh` with a footer that rotates through a curated list of 10 wavemill usage tips selected at random on each render tick.

### Why

The current footer reads `Refreshes every 2s │ Ctrl+B <PANE>: switch task │ Ctrl+B N: next done` and never changes. Users miss non-obvious wavemill functionality (auto-cleanup of merged windows, auto-merge of ready tasks, CLI access to expand/plan/eval, dashboard refresh tuning, project-context compaction, permission auto-approve). A rotating tip surface acts as a low-cost in-product discovery channel and shortens the learning curve for power features.

### Scope In

* Curate exactly 10 short, accurate wavemill usage tips (≤ 100 chars each, single-line).
* Implement a rotation mechanism that selects one tip per dashboard render tick.
* Preserve the "Refreshes every Ns" segment (or equivalent indicator) so users still see refresh cadence.
* Update the rendering function in `shared/lib/wavemill-status.sh` to emit the rotating line.
* Add a shell test fixture that asserts list integrity (length, max char width, distinctness) and rotation behavior.
* Update `docs/mill-mode.md` with a short note about the rotating tips footer.

### Scope Out

* No new config keys to opt out of rotation (out of scope; can be added later if users request).
* No telemetry on which tip was shown.
* No localization/i18n of tip strings.
* No animated/marquee scrolling — tips swap atomically per refresh.
* No changes to the dashboard layout above the footer line (panes, headers, status indicators).
* No changes to the `USR1` signal-driven refresh path beyond what is necessary for rotation.

---

## 2\. Technical Context

### Repository

This repository (`wavemill`).

### Key Files

* `shared/lib/wavemill-status.sh` — renders dashboard status; owns the current static footer line. Modify to emit rotating tip.
* `shared/lib/wavemill-mill.sh` — orchestrates mill-mode dashboard refresh loop; verify no changes needed but read for refresh-cycle context.
* `shared/lib/wavemill-common.sh` — shared shell helpers; if a tip list helper is needed it can live here, but prefer co-locating with `wavemill-status.sh`.
* `tests/wavemill-status.test.sh` — existing dashboard test file; add new test cases here.
* `tests/check-shell.sh` — shellcheck runner that gates shell changes (must continue to pass).
* `docs/mill-mode.md` — user-facing docs; append short section describing rotating tips.

### Relevant Subsystem Specs

⚠️ **Knowledge Gap**: No subsystem spec was found for the wavemill dashboard / status rendering subsystem. The provided specs (`router.md`, `eval-system.md`, `quota-tracking.md`) are unrelated to this change. After implementation, consider running `npx tsx tools/init-project-context.ts --force` (or `wavemill context init --force` if available) to create a `wavemill-dashboard` subsystem spec capturing footer rendering, refresh cadence, and `USR1` signaling so future tasks in this area benefit from cold-memory context.

### Dependencies

* POSIX shell + bash features already used by `wavemill-status.sh`.
* `$RANDOM` (bash built-in) for tip selection — already commonly available; no new external dependency.
* No new npm/tsx tools required.

### Architecture Notes

* The dashboard supports `USR1`-driven immediate refresh in addition to a poll fallback (default 2s, configurable via `WAVEMILL_DASHBOARD_REFRESH_SECONDS`, valid range 1–10). The rotating-tip implementation MUST select the tip *during* a render pass, not in a background process, so that each render is self-contained and the `USR1` fast-path remains correct.
* Atomic writes / single-writer patterns are used elsewhere (`/tmp/wavemill-*.hook`). Footer rendering does not write state, so no locking is needed.
* Tips are presentation strings only — do NOT make them depend on runtime state (e.g., do not show "auto-cleanup is on" based on config). That would couple rotation to config reads on every refresh tick.

---

## 3\. Implementation Approach

1. **Locate the existing footer line.** Open `shared/lib/wavemill-status.sh` and find the literal string `Refreshes every` (or similar) that emits `Refreshes every 2s │ Ctrl+B <PANE>: switch task │ Ctrl+B N: next done`. Confirm this is the only render site; grep the repo to be sure.
2. **Define the tip list.** Add a bash array `WAVEMILL_DASHBOARD_TIPS` (or a function returning the list) inside `wavemill-status.sh` containing the 10 curated tips below. Keep each tip ≤ 100 chars.
3. **Implement selection.** Add a helper `wavemill_dashboard_pick_tip()` that selects `WAVEMILL_DASHBOARD_TIPS[$((RANDOM % ${#WAVEMILL_DASHBOARD_TIPS[@]}))]` and echoes it. The selection happens once per render call.
4. **Compose the footer.** Replace the static footer string with `Refreshes every ${REFRESH}s │ Tip: <selected tip>`. Keep the refresh indicator so the cadence remains visible. Drop the literal `Ctrl+B <PANE>: switch task │ Ctrl+B N: next done` from the static slot (those two specific hints can become two of the rotating tips so they are not lost).
5. **Verify single-line width.** Ensure the longest composed line fits within typical pane widths. If the dashboard footer truncates at a known width elsewhere, respect it.
6. **Update tests.** In `tests/wavemill-status.test.sh`, add cases asserting:
   * `WAVEMILL_DASHBOARD_TIPS` has exactly 10 entries.
   * No duplicate entries.
   * Every entry is ≤ 100 chars.
   * Calling the render function repeatedly with a forced `RANDOM` seed produces deterministic, varying outputs.
7. **Run shellcheck.** Ensure new code passes `tests/check-shell.sh`.
8. **Update docs.** Add a short paragraph to `docs/mill-mode.md` under the dashboard section describing the rotating tip footer.
9. **Commit & PR.** Single focused commit referencing HOK-1626.

### Curated Tips (10)

Each is a draft — verify accuracy against the codebase before merging. Each is single-line and ≤ 100 chars.

 1. `Tip: Ctrl+B <PANE>: switch task │ Ctrl+B N: next done — navigate the mill dashboard`
 2. `Tip: Set WAVEMILL_DASHBOARD_REFRESH_SECONDS=1..10 to tune dashboard refresh cadence`
 3. `Tip: Run 'wavemill expand <ISSUE>' to turn a Linear issue into a task packet from the CLI`
 4. `Tip: Run 'wavemill plan' to decompose an initiative into sub-issues without entering mill mode`
 5. `Tip: Run 'wavemill eval <PR>' to score a merged PR against the eval rubric from the CLI`
 6. `Tip: SKIP_CONTEXT_CHECK=true wavemill mill — skip the project-context init prompt on startup`
 7. `Tip: 'npx tsx tools/compact-project-context.ts' compacts .wavemill/project-context.md when it grows`
 8. `Tip: Configure .wavemill-config.json → permissions.autoApprovePatterns to silence read-only prompts`
 9. `Tip: 'npx tsx tools/init-project-context.ts --force' regenerates subsystem specs in .wavemill/context/`
10. `Tip: 'npx tsx tools/get-backlog.ts "Project Name"' fetches the Linear backlog from the CLI`

**Note**: Tip #1 preserves the keyboard navigation hint that previously lived in the static footer.

---

## 4\. Success Criteria

### Functional Requirements

- [ ] **\[REQ-F1\]** Dashboard footer no longer shows the static string `Refreshes every 2s │ Ctrl+B <PANE>: switch task │ Ctrl+B N: next done`; instead it shows `Refreshes every Ns │ Tip: <one of 10 tips>`.
- [ ] **\[REQ-F2\]** The tip list contains exactly 10 distinct tips, each ≤ 100 characters, no leading/trailing whitespace, no embedded newlines.
- [ ] **\[REQ-F3\]** Tip selection occurs per render tick (each invocation of the footer rendering function selects a tip via `RANDOM`); over many invocations all 10 tips have non-zero probability of being shown.
- [ ] **\[REQ-F4\]** Refresh cadence indicator continues to reflect the effective refresh interval (default 2s, or the value of `WAVEMILL_DASHBOARD_REFRESH_SECONDS` if set in the 1–10 range).
- [ ] **\[REQ-F5\]** Every tip in the list is factually correct: every referenced command (e.g., `wavemill expand`, `wavemill plan`, `wavemill eval`, `npx tsx tools/...`), env var (e.g., `WAVEMILL_DASHBOARD_REFRESH_SECONDS`, `SKIP_CONTEXT_CHECK`), and config key (e.g., `permissions.autoApprovePatterns`) is verifiable against the current codebase.

### Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] Footer line width ≤ 100 characters in worst case (longest tip + cadence prefix).
- [ ] No measurable change in dashboard refresh latency vs. baseline (rotation is O(1) bash array index).
- [ ] No new external dependencies; uses bash built-ins only.

### Code Quality

- [ ] Follows existing shell-script patterns in `shared/lib/wavemill-status.sh`.
- [ ] Passes `tests/check-shell.sh` (shellcheck).
- [ ] No lint errors.

---

## 5\. Implementation Constraints

* **Code style**: Match existing `shared/lib/wavemill-status.sh` shell conventions (function naming, quoting, `set -euo pipefail` usage if present).
* **Testing**: Use the existing bash test harness in `tests/wavemill-status.test.sh`. Force `RANDOM` via seed (`RANDOM=42`) to make rotation tests deterministic.
* **Security**: Tip strings are static literals; no user input is interpolated into the footer. Do not source tips from any external file at runtime.
* **Performance**: Selection must be O(1) and must not fork external processes or read files on every render tick.
* **Backwards compatibility**: No config keys are added or removed. Users who scripted around the literal old footer string (unlikely) will see a different line — document this in the PR description.
* **No state coupling**: Rotation must not read config, hook files, or quota state. It must be a pure render-time pick from a static array.
* **Width**: Each tip ≤ 100 chars; combined footer line ≤ 110 chars.

---

## 6\. Validation Steps

### Functional Requirement Validation

**\[REQ-F1\] Dashboard footer shows rotating tip, not the static string**

1. Setup: Check out the branch, run the dashboard in a controlled harness (or invoke the footer render function directly from a test).
2. Action: Invoke the footer render function 20 times.
3. Expected result: Each invocation prints a line of the form `Refreshes every <N>s │ Tip: <tip text>`; the legacy string `Ctrl+B N: next done` does not appear as a *static* tail — it appears only when tip #1 is selected.
4. Edge cases:
   * `WAVEMILL_DASHBOARD_REFRESH_SECONDS=5` set → cadence segment reads `Refreshes every 5s`.
   * `WAVEMILL_DASHBOARD_REFRESH_SECONDS=999` (invalid) set → cadence falls back to `2s` (per existing behavior documented in CLAUDE.md).

**\[REQ-F2\] Tip list integrity**

1. Setup: Source `shared/lib/wavemill-status.sh` in a test shell.
2. Action: Inspect `WAVEMILL_DASHBOARD_TIPS` (or the equivalent accessor).
3. Expected result: `${#WAVEMILL_DASHBOARD_TIPS[@]}` equals `10`; sorted unique count also equals `10`; max `awk '{print length}'` over entries ≤ `100`.
4. Edge cases:
   * Adding an 11th entry → test fails with explicit count mismatch.
   * Adding a duplicate → test fails with duplicate-detection message.
   * Adding a 101-char entry → test fails with width violation.

**\[REQ-F3\] Rotation visits all tips over many invocations**

1. Setup: Seed `RANDOM` deterministically (`RANDOM=1`); call the picker N=1000 times collecting output.
2. Action: Count distinct tips observed.
3. Expected result: All 10 tips appear at least once; distribution is roughly uniform (no tip with > 25% or < 5% frequency for N=1000).
4. Edge cases:
   * `RANDOM=0` seed → still produces valid selections, no off-by-one (index in `[0,9]`).
   * 1 invocation only → exactly one tip is emitted, no error.

**\[REQ-F4\] Refresh cadence indicator preserved**

1. Setup: Unset `WAVEMILL_DASHBOARD_REFRESH_SECONDS`.
2. Action: Render footer once; capture output.
3. Expected result: Prefix reads `Refreshes every 2s │ Tip: …`.
4. Edge cases:
   * `WAVEMILL_DASHBOARD_REFRESH_SECONDS=1` → prefix is `Refreshes every 1s`.
   * `WAVEMILL_DASHBOARD_REFRESH_SECONDS=10` → prefix is `Refreshes every 10s`.

# HOK-1626: Rotating usage tips at bottom of Dashboard.

# Rotating Usage Tips at Bottom of Dashboard - Quick Reference

**Issue ID**: HOK-1626

## Objective

Replace the static dashboard footer line ("Refreshes every 2s │ Ctrl+B <PANE>: switch task │ Ctrl+B N: next done") with a rotating selection from a curated list of 10 wavemill usage tips. Each refresh cycle randomly chooses a tip to surface non-obvious functionality (auto-cleanup, auto-merge, CLI commands, config options) to users. Keep the existing refresh/keyboard hints somewhere visible while rotating the rest.

## Key Files

* `shared/lib/wavemill-status.sh` — dashboard footer rendering (status/help line)
* `shared/lib/wavemill-mill.sh` — mill-mode dashboard composition
* `shared/lib/wavemill-common.sh` — shared helpers used by status rendering
* `tests/wavemill-status.test.sh` — dashboard rendering tests
* `docs/mill-mode.md` — user-facing documentation for mill dashboard

## Critical Constraints

1. **Each tip must fit on a single line** at typical terminal widths (≤ 100 chars including separators) — no wrapping in dashboard footer.
2. **Tips must be factually accurate** — every command, flag, or config key must be verifiable against the current codebase (e.g., `WAVEMILL_DASHBOARD_REFRESH_SECONDS`, `wavemill expand`, `.wavemill-config.json` keys).
3. **Rotation must not destabilize the dashboard** — selection happens per render tick and must be deterministic-per-tick (no flicker mid-render), and must not break the existing `USR1`-driven refresh path.

## Success Criteria (High-Level)

- [ ] Static footer line is replaced by a rotating tip selected from a curated list of 10 tips.
- [ ] Each tip is short, accurate, and surfaces non-obvious wavemill functionality.
- [ ] Dashboard refresh cadence and `USR1` signal-driven updates continue to work unchanged.
- [ ] Tests cover tip list integrity (count, length, no duplicates) and rotation behavior.
- [ ] Tests and shellcheck pass; PR created and linked to HOK-1626.

## Detailed Sections
